threads.subject: [URGENT] Worker/ student -> out of status -> restore to visitor? -- REP-2020-2199
threads.question:
Hello,
Initial Question (REP-2020-2497): IRCC authorizes out-of-status students to apply for a post-graduation work permit by including restoration fees with their PGWP application.
Would IRCC similarly authorize an out-of-status student to apply for an LMIA-exempt open work permit (specifically under LMIA exemption codes C-42 or C-41) by including a restoration to student fee receipt with their application? If not, what would be the correct procedure?
Response: Study permit holders who do not apply for a PGWP before their study permit expires would be in Canada without a valid status. Their temporary resident status would need to be restored as a student before they can be issued a PGWP. In this situation, the procedure is to submit an application to restore status as a student and apply for a PGWP simultaneously and submit their proof of completion of studies and transcripts instead of their old letter of acceptance (please note that a new letter of acceptance is not required). Note that they must pay the fees for a new study permit and a work permit, which will include restoration fee ($200), study permit fee ($150), work permit fee ($155) and open work permit holder fee ($100).
As the applications are submitted simultaneously, they are processed together at the processing center. As such, a decision on the Post-Graduation Work permit will be rendered likely on the same day as the study permit, unless additional documents are required.
Please note that an applicant may only restore to an authorization that they held immediately prior to the restoration application, as per section 182 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. In the case of an out-of-status student, the applicant may only restore their authorization to study and not to work. As well as the study permit fee, the applicant must also submit the standard application package for a study permit (Please see Guide 5552 - Applying to Change Conditions or Extend Your Stay in Canada-Student).
The applicant may also choose to submit an application for a work permit under a different category instead of applying for a PGWP (e.g. one under LMIA exemption code C41 or C42) at the same time if they qualify for another type of work permit. If an officer determines that the applicant is eligible for restoration as a student, only then will they assess the work permit application.
For more information, please see: Restoration of temporary resident status
Follow-up Question (REP-2020-2592): There is conflicting information available regarding whether a foreign national who held status as a worker/student when he/she fell out of status eligible to restore their status to visitor?
If so, are two forms required? i.e. in the worker scenario, both application form for restoration as worker (IMM5710) and visitor (IMM5708) are required to be submitted via portal and the fees paid twice?
In the past, CPC-E has approved applications corresponding to the above-mentioned scenarios with only the submission of
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
the application for restoration as a visitor (IMM5708). However, the current restoration guidelines, modified on April 8, 2020, state that "a foreign national can only apply to restore their status and authorization to one they held immediately prior to the need to apply for restoration."
Please confirm if these guidelines now preclude restoring to a lower status and if not, how many forms are required to be submitted.
Response: Please note that when a temporary resident submits an application to restore their stay as a worker or student, the client is effectively submitting two applications in one; the first is to restore their status as a temporary resident while the second is to seek an authorization as a worker or student. The program delivery instructions regarding restoration (linked above)
specify the following:
It is important to note that an applicant can only restore to an authorization that they held immediately prior to the restoration application. As an example, a student who lost their status cannot apply to restore status with authorization as a worker.
A restoration application is submitted with the purpose of restoring the applicant's status as a temporary resident; as per the above, they are limited to seek their authorization (i.e. as a worker or student) to what they previously held. An out-of-status worker or student may apply to restore their status as a visitor without submitting an application (and the associated fees) for a work or study permit. However, restoring their status as a visitor may limit them to later apply for a work or study permit from inside Canada.

Hello – to confirm your hypothetical scenario is: a temporary foreign worker in Canada whose work permit expires on May 31,
2021. All immigration decisions are made after this date. It is important to remember that status and authorization are two separate things under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations. QUESTION: PART 1: both applications are sent prior to the expiry of the temporary stay-Tab 1 & Tab 2 Tab 2, question 1 : even though the FN now has a visitor record, can you confirm that they maintain the authorization to work under R1 83(5) until a decision is made on their WP application? RESPONSE: As indicated in the Program Delivery Instructions Pending decision on work permit renewal [R186(u)] : A foreign national who submits the form Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710] to renew their work permit may be submitting two applications in one. The temporary resident is applying under section R181 for an “extension of authorization to remain" and under section R201 to "renew the work permit". If submitted before the expiry of their current work permit, this combined application has 3 effects:
1. Should a final decision not be made on the application under section R181 before the expiration of their current status, the temporary resident's status will be maintained by law under subsection R183(5).
2. The application for renewal under section R201 allows the foreign national to work without a permit under paragraph R186(u) until a decision is made, unless they leave Canada or fail to comply with conditions imposed.
3. Any conditions imposed on the current work permit carry over to the work without a permit period under paragraph R186(u)
If the work permit holder is changing from a work permit to just a visitor, then R201 does not apply and therefore, an application to extend only as a visitor does not meet the requirements to work without a permit under R186(u). An application for a Visitor extension only would only be under R181 and therefore only meet the requirements for an extension of the period of authorized stay under R183(5). It does not provide any authority to work without a permit or continue working in any other way.
The work permit renewal application submitted under R201 is what would allow the applicant to meet the requirements to work without a permit under R186(u) pending a decision on the work permit application.
If these two different applications were submitted at the same time and the Visitor extension application is approved first, then the period of authorized stay is extended to the date of validity on the Visitor record and the authorization to work without a permit under R186(u) is maintained until a decision on the work permit.

The applicant can no longer continue working under R186(u) as a decision on the work permit has been made.
However, the second application submitted under R181 before the period of authorized stay under R183(5) expired, provides for a continued period of authorized stay until a decision is made on the second application.
It should be noted that there are two different expiry periods that must be taken into account. In order to apply for an extension of authorization and benefit from the extension of period of authorized stay under R183(5) the application under R181 must be made 'before the period of authorized stay ends'. However, for the authority to work without a permit under R186(u), the work permit renewal application under R201 must be made before the work permit expires.
Tab 4, question 4-has the same answer as above: If second application (Visitor Record) for extension is submitted during the period of authorized stay and the Visitor extension application is approved first, then the period of authorized stay is extended to the date of validity on the Visitor record and the authorization to work without a permit under R186(u) is maintained until a decision on the work permit.
QUESTlON: PART 3: visitor record application sent prior to the expiry of the temporary stay, work permit sent during the period of extended authorized stay (R183(5)) and before a decision is made on visitor record application-Tab 5 &Tab 6 Tab 5, question 5: based on your wording online the FN is authorized to stay even if the VR application was refused. authorization to stay until the decision on the last application is made?
RESPoNSE: Please note that if the application for an extension of status (Visitor Record) is submitted under R181 first it only allows for the extension of the period of authorized stay and does not provide any authority to contine working. This information is found in the Program Delivery Instruction: Pending decision on work permit renewal [R186(u)]. For a subsequent work permit application to be submitted under R200 (it is not a renewal under R201), the applicant must meet the requirements of R199 for application after entry to Canada.

Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Good day,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox. Due to the impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on our operations, we have experienced delays in providing a response.
We understand that Covid-19 has made it more difficult for many applicants to submit documents that IRCC requires in a timely fashion. As a result, IRCC will normally accept forms with photocopies or scans of wet (handwritten) signatures. However, a client may be asked to provide the original copy of their forms with an original signature if an IRCC officer determines it is necessary.
In regards to remote commissioning, as a result of Covid-19, the Federal Court of Canada has adopted a policy of allowing remotely commissioned statutory declarations and affidavits. Because of this, IRCC currently permits remote commissioning for the following form: Application for authorization and statutory declaration (IMM 0006). By extension, IRCC would generally allow remote commissioning during Covid-19 for the Statutory Declaration of Common-law Union IMM 5409, provided that the lawyer or commissioner of oaths could watch the client sign the statutory declaration through video. The client would then scan and send the signed document electronically to the lawyer or commissioner of oaths, who would then sign it as well, and submit to IRCC (either electronically, or by mail). It should be noted that the witnessing official must be Canadian certified to ensure they are legally authorized to receive a solemn declaration. Should the officer have concerns that the solemn declaration was not conducted through video or does not contain photocopied or scanned copies of the wet signatures, the officer may contact the client for further information.
We hope you find this information useful.
Thank you,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox (IRCC)

have valid status in Canada as a visitor on the day they apply
have remained in Canada with valid status

threads.answer:
Good day,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox. Due to the impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on our operations, we have experienced delays in providing a response.
As you have mentioned, IRCC deems the Somali passport unreliable and not valid for travel to Canada. An alternative solution would be for the family member to obtain a valid travel document. This would be an identity document issued by an international organization (such as the United Nations) that would contain the individual's photograph, personal information, and allow that individual to travel between countries.
A sponsor and their family member(s) must meet all of the applicable requirements as set out in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and it's applicable Regulations (IRPR). This includes meeting the requirement stipulated in section 50(1) of the IRPR. Foreign nationals who do not meet the requirements of the IRPA or the IRPR may make a written request for consideration under subsection A25(1) for humanitarian and compassionate considerations. The foreign national would need to provide a written request along with their family class application in order to be considered under these grounds. Requests for humanitarian and compassionate considerations are assessed on a case- by-case basis. This means that the deciding officer will assess the request and all the relevant information in order to determine whether a special grant of an exemption from a requirement of the IRPA or IRPR is warranted. For more detailed information on humanitarian and compassionate considerations, you may wish to consult the following website: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-) bulletins-manuals/permanent-residence/humanitarian-compassionate-consideration/intake-who-may-apply.html.

Good Day,

mailbox.
Question Retail butchers are one of the eligible occupations under the Agri-Food Pilot Project. Do retail butchers working for supermarket meat/butcher departments qualify? My concern is whether a supermarket/employer is considered to be operating under NAICS 3116, one of the eligible industries under the Pilot. NAICS 3116 is comprised of "establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing meat products". The typical supermarket meat department is engaged in processing of meat products, including receiving animal carcasses and butchering the carcasses into consumer-friendly cuts. However, typical supermarkets also sell produce and other non-meat food products.
[https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb/p3VD.pl?](https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb/p3VD.pl?) Function=getVD&TVD= &CVD= &CPV=3116&CST=01012012&CLV=3&MLV=5
Answer
Applicants applying to the Agri-Food Pilot (AFP) program will need to demonstrate that they meet the minimum work experience requirement in one or more eligible combinations of the National Occupational Classification (NOC) and North American Industry Classification System (NAICS). Activities under eligible industry NAICS 3116 (Meat product manufacturing) lists the eligible occupation NOC 6331 (Butchers, meat cutter, and fishmongers in retail and wholesale). That said, grocery stores and supermarkets fall under NAICS 4451 which is not eligible under the AFP program.
Please note that the officer would need to be satisfied that the applicant has performed the main job duties, including all of the essential duties listed under the NOC 6331 and that the employer's principal business activity is consistent with NAICS 3116.

threads.answer:
Hello,
Please see our response to your question.
Question: If an applicant obtains a LMIA exempt work permit restricted to a city (e.g. Montreal) but want to move to another city that is not in the same administrative region (e.g.), what would be the best way forward? Would they require a new work permit?
The employer operates an office in the city mentioned on the work permit and the employee will be working remotely for the employer within the same provide.
Please confirm how to proceed in situations like this as we believe this is something that we might see more and more.
Answer: There are two sets of conditions to consider in employment location – those imposed on the employee under section 185 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) and those imposed on the employer under 209.3 of the IRPR. If the location is imposed on the work permit, the foreign worker must change their conditions to move locations.
For foreign workers working remotely on a temporary basis due to the Covid situation, it is recommended that employers submit a voluntary disclosure to notify IRCC of the changes.
For scenarios where an employer wishes to make teleworking permanent and valid post-Covid, we recommend that the employer submit a new offer of employment and have the worker submit an application to change conditions as a worker.
We would also recommend that employers include teleworking arrangement information in any new offer of employment. The employer is also required to maintain any documentation regarding the changes and provide it as justification at the time of inspection.
If the employer believes that they are not meeting conditions, they can use the voluntary disclosure process.
We hope this information is of assistance.

threads.subject: Visiting Professors -- REP-2021-0240
threads.question:
Hello,
If a visiting professor with a work permit under LMiA exemption code C22 has worked in Canada for two years, are they eligible to apply for a work permit under the same category if they have left Canada for one year?
Thank you and I look forward to your response.
Kind regards,
Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Dear
Question: If a visiting professor with a work permit under LMlA exemption code C22 has worked in Canada for two years, are they eligible to apply for a work permit under the same category if they have left Canada for one year?
Response: Work permits for visiting professors are authorised for a maximum period of two academic years, however the guidelines are silent on the length of time between visits to Canada under this category. If a foreign national seeks to return to Canada under LMlA exemption C22 at a later time, they must be able to satisfy the processing officer that an exchange still exists and remains temporary in nature. The onus is on the foreign national to demonstrate the temporary nature of their intended stay in Canada.
The limit of two years is in place to reinforce the temporary nature of these opportunities and mitigates potential impacts on Canadians' access to academic teaching opportunities.

threads.subject: Subject: Clarification on police clearance from Nepal - -REP-2021-0414
threads.question:
and Cizenship Canedaot Cioyenneté Canada
Hello,
I had a question on clarification on police clearance from Nepal.
Scenario: Principal Applicant (PA) holds Nepalese passport. Applying for PR under EE CEC. PA has received ITA on March 18,
2021. PA has applied for PCC online directly from Police Headquarters, Kathmandu because the Nepalese Embassy in Ottawa doesn't process PCC from Canada.
The issue is that this person's FSW EE was rejected by IRCC in 2019 on the same grounds. IRCC rejected PCC on these grounds, "The Police certificate from Nepal was issued prior to your last residence in that country. The Police certificate was issued on 2018/12/28. Your last residence in this country was 2018/12/29.
This time again, the PCC received from Nepal was issued one day before the PA left Nepal. PA boarded the flight on Dec 29th, 2018 (evening flight). PCC is issued till Dec 28, 2018. PCC states, 'He has no criminal record against him till 28th December 2018, as verified from central police crime database’.
1. PA has contacted the Nepalese Embassy in Ottawa via email to get this documented but they don't reply. Embassy telephonically told them to apply from Nepal.
2. Local police in Nepal state that this is the format that they issue & cannot change it. They just see the departure stamp on the PP & issue the PCC a day earlier. Again, no reply to email communication.
Question: What is the solution here?
Regards,
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for your email correspondence.
to 's (IRCC) Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Based on the information provided, it appears that (IRCC) had reviewed your client's application for permanent residence and determined that the application did not meet the requirements of a complete application as described in sections 10 and 12.01 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. As a result, the application was rejected for being incomplete since the Police Certificate from Nepal provided in support of the
application did not cover the full period of time spent in Nepal.
If this is indeed the case, you may wish to submit a Reconsideration Request to the Centralized Intake Office (ClO), in Sydney,
Nova Scotia and request that IRCC further examine and reopen the application.
In exceptional circumstances, IRCC may accept both of the following:
proof of having requested a police certificate for some countries; and an explanation of best efforts (not a guarantee of acceptance) In this explanation, the applicant should explain the circumstances or the delay in the document. The uploaded document must show that the applicant requested a police certificate as soon as possible after receiving their invitation to apply; Submit the flight itinerary/ticket proving that your client boarded the flight on the 29th of December of 2018; Provide a scanned copy of exit stamps from Nepal and entry stamps to Canada; oAn explanation detailing your client's best efforts made to obtain an updated police certificate including any communication between the client and the Nepalese Embassy in Ottawa, as well as any dealings with the local police in Kathmandu, Nepal.
Otherwise, you are welcome to reapply if you feel that you can respond to the outlined concerns and can demonstrate that your situation meets the requirements. All new applications must be accompanied by a new processing fee.

Answer: If the applicant obtains permanent residence through Express Entry, their SUV application will be withdrawn. If the applicant was deemed an “essential" person under the SUV application, the remaining SUV candidates would be refused for not meeting the requirements to be a member of the start-up business class. The remaining applicants may need to provide a new Commitment Certificate and Letter of Support, and additional documentation noting the changes in ownership and shareholders.
The assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: If the applicant works under two CNPs for one week, for example, 20 hrs as a professor with employer A, 10 hrs as an admin assistant with employer B. Can he sum up the work hours for these two jobs?
Answer: Yes, applicant must have at least 12 months of full-time, Canadian skilled work experience (or the equivalent in part-time work experience) in one or more NOC 0, A or B occupations within the 36 months before the date of application receipt. Applicants can work as many part-time jobs as needed to meet this requirement. Please note that we do not count any hours worked over 30 hours/week. Additional information is available on our website. The skilled work experience must be paid work, including paid wages or earned commission.
Question: Someone has worked full time as a research assistant (4012) in a University in Canada on a valid work permit. However, he was receiving a postdoctoral fellowship from his own country and it is the only resource of revenue, will this work experience be recognized under CEC?
Answer: Any period of employment when the applicant was engaged in full-time study will not be included in calculating the period of qualifying work experience as per 87.1(3)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (e.g., work experience gained through co-op work permits, off-campus work permits while a full-time student and on-campus work permits). The skilled work experience must also be paid work, including paid wages or earned commission.
Question: To extend the above question, if someone has worked physically in Canada for 12 months on a work permit (for example, PGWP), full time, 0, A, B, has the required language abilities, however, his employer is a foreign company based outside of Canada and He was being paid by this foreign employer outside of Canada, will this period of work experience be recognized under CEC?
Answer: Work performed while in the employ of a foreign employer, despite being performed physically in Canada, could be considered foreign or Canadian work experience depending on the circumstances of the case as a whole. The applicant's presence in Canada does not preclude this from being considered foreign work experience and the source of remuneration is not the only determining factor. An officer however, will make the final assessment based on the information available.
Question: The applicant has worked for an employer listed/specified on the work permit on a closed work permit for 12 months in Canada. This employer (who has a few branches across Canada) is ready to offer the applicant a full-time job for at least one year once he's accepted as a permanent resident for his other branch located in another province. Assuming, the applicants meet the other criteria, will this job offer be accepted as a valid job offer under Express Entry?
Answer: Yes, the applicant would receive CRS points for arranged employment as long as they continue to meet the requirements stated under section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system. Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient
documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.

Answer: No, it is not mandatory for the applicant to be on a work permit to claim arranged employment points. Question:
An applicant completes a three-year college program in Canada. Subsequently, they complete a bachelor’s degree outside of Canada. They receive an educational credential assessment for that degree which states it is from a recognized institution and is equivalent to a Canadian degree. Credits from the college degree are applied towards the bachelor's degree, allowing the applicant to complete the degree in less than the standard amount of time (say two years instead of three).
How many points would be awarded for education? Would it be based on a bachelor's degree, (120 points if single) or on ‘Two or more certificates, diplomas, or degrees. One must be for a program of three or more years' (128 points if single).
Answer:
A candidate will only be awarded education points under the Comprehensive Ranking System and the Federal Skilled Worker selection grid for having 'two or more post-secondary program credentials' if the educational credentials represent separate certificates, diplomas or degrees. To get points for having two or more post-secondary credentials, at least one of the credentials must be for three or more years of study.
Based on the information provided, the applicant should declare only a single post-secondary program credential of three years or more. This is because they did not complete a three year program then another program. The first program became the Bachelor's. Therefore, the applicant should input only their Bachelor's Degree and the appropriate points will be awarded.
We trust that this information will assist you.

threads.subject: Are clinical or post-doctoral fellows considered to be working in Canada for CEC purposes? -- REP-2021-0247
threads.question:
1*1and Cizenship Canada
Dear Imm Reps,
If a foreign national holds an LMIA exempt work permit for a one-year post-doctoral medical fellowship or post-doctoral fellow and his full salary is paid by his home country, will his work experience count as a Canadian work experience under the EE-CEC?
Kind regards,
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question: If a foreign national holds an LMIA exempt work permit for a one-year post-doctoral medical fellowship or post-doctoral fellow and his full salary is paid by his home country, will his work experience count as a Canadian work experience under the EE-CEC?
Answer:
A foreign national who holds a work permit under LMIA-exemption code C45 for a one-year post-doctoral medical fellowship is considered to be working. Under the International Mobility Program which covers C45, the foreign national is part of the Canadian labour force despite the lack of a Labour Market Impact Assessment.
Work is defined in Section 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Regulations: Despite the definition work in section 2, for the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned.
While a fellowship may be considered work for the purposes of their work permit, please note that if they are receiving a stipend or allowance, where the primary purpose is to cover expenses, this would not generally be considered wages (and therefore the work would not count for permanent residence). The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer that there was the payment of wages.
If all requirements are met, then the activity would count as qualifying Canadian work experience for the purposes of applying for permanent residence.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

According to our PDI, foreign nationals are required to obtain a study permit for engaging in academic, professional, vocational or other education or training in Canada that is more than 6 months in duration. As per paragraph 216(e) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), the issuance of study permits is limited to applicants who have been accepted to undertake a program of study at a designated learning institution (DLl). Therefore, a foreign national may not undertake studies for which a study permit is required at an institution that is not a DLI.

- courses of general interest or self-improvement
- distance learning audited courses (typically by sitting in on an academic course but without obtaining credit for it or having the ability to obtain credit for it retroactively)

The ministerial instructions on the IRCC website for Express Entry outlines the requirement to earn a Canadian degree, diploma, or certificate:

mmigration, Réfugiés
1. For Express Entry, there have been no changes to how CRS points are awarded for education. A Canadian educational credential cannot be awarded if the credentials were obtained in a study or training program in which distance learning amounted to more than half of the program length. To get points the credential must be a “Canadian educational credential," as per R73 and meet one of the definitions of an, Eligible credential”. Pursuant to R73.1, a Canadian educational credential means any diploma, certificate or credential, issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions. In addition, the credential must meet the requirements stated in the Express Entry Ministerial Instructions — MI 1 1(3) and MI 30 (1)-(5).

A period of employment during which time the foreign national was engaged in full-time study will not count as Canadian work experience’ for the purposes of points assigned under the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS). 1. on an employer specific work permit, and
2. while studying as a PhD
counts as Canadian work experience under Express Entry?
Kind regards,
Answer:
Work experience, while studying as a full time student in Canada, can not be claimed for Express Entry points and can not count towards CRS points.
To apply for permanent residence under the Canadian Experience Class, the foreign worker skilled work experience must:
* be in a job classified as skill type 0, or skill level A or B according to the 2016 National Occupational Classification,
* amount to at least one year of full-time (or an equal amount in part-time) in the previous three years,
* have been with an employer in Canada (self-employment does not count),
* be gained with the proper legal authorization (for example, as a documented worker with a valid work permit), and
* not be gained while the foreign worker was studying on a student permit. If the client provides a letter from the school stating that they’re not studying full time, the work experience may be considered. As always, the onus is on the applicant to provide the appropriate documentation. At time of assessment, the IRCC reviewing officer will use their discretion when evaluating information and supporting documents in the application. We trust that this information will assist you. threads.subject: Question about Cannabis Possession & Criminal Inadmissibility -- REP-2021-0429
threads.question:
Hello Mr
Thank you for reaching out to Immigration Representatives Mailbox.
As of October 17, 2018, simple possession of cannabis (up to 30 grams) from a legal source is not a criminal offence in Canada and would not render a foreign national inadmissible for criminality under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). However, if there is evidence that it was illicit cannabis (for example, obtained from an illegal source), the individual would be inadmissible. Equally, knowingly possessing illicit cannabis in any amount is considered illegal. The same applies to convictions or offences committed outside Canada; simple possession from a legal source does not render a foreign national inadmissible for criminality. However, if there is evidence that it was obtained from an illegal source, the individual would be inadmissible.
Generally speaking, if the Canadian conviction is no longer a crime in Canada at the time of the inadmissibility determination, the person is not inadmissible for that crime. Similarly, if the foreign offence is no longer a crime in Canada, the person is not inadmissible for that crime.
For more information about how marijuana related penalties could affect an individual's immigration status, please visit : [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/impaired-driving-cannabis-penalties-affect-immigration-status.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/impaired-driving-cannabis-penalties-affect-immigration-status.html)
We trust that this information will be useful to you. Please let us know if you have any further questions.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: refugee claimants and implied status -- REP-2021-0411
threads.question:
Dear officer,
With respect to a refugee claimant who holds an open work permit based on their refugee status, does this applicant benefit from the implied status rules? So if they apply for a new open work permit (based on their refugee status) before their current open work permit (that was issued based on their refugee status) expires can they continue to work on
implied status? Or must they stop working until they receive their new open work permit?
Thank you.
threads.answer:
Good day
Thank you for reaching out to us with your inquiry, you will find the answers below.
Question 1
With respect to a refugee claimant who holds an open work permit based on their refugee status, does this applicant benefit from the implied status rules?
Answer1 A foreign national in Canada who has made a claim to refugee status loses their status upon the determination of an officer that they are in non-compliance as per section 47 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). Therefore, they have no status as of that point. The work permit issued under section 206 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) does not confer status as per section 202 of the IRPR. If the foreign national does not meet any of the requirements for the ability to work without a permit under section 186 of the IRPR, then they have no authority to work if they do not hold a
valid work permit.
Question 2 So if they apply for a new open work permit (based on their refugee status) before their current open work permit (that was issued based on their refugee status) expires can they continue to work on implied status? Or must they stop working until they receive their new open work permit?
Answer2 As there are no status maintained, the applicant must stop working until they receive a valid work permit.
We trust you will find this information useful.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Question relative au lieu de travail apparaissant sur un permis de travail -- REP-2021-0547
threads.question:
# Bonjour,
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
Dans le cas d’un employé dont la ville de son employeur apparait comme lieu de travail sur son permis de travail peut-il effectuer du télétravail à partir de son domicile situé dans une autre ville sans contrevenir aux conditions énoncées à son permis? Existe-t-il une tolérance à ce niveau ou une demande de changement des conditions du permis de travail doit-elle plutôt être faite pour ajouter cet autre lieu de travail qui est son domicile?
Est-ce que la réponse est la même selon que l’on se situe en période de crise sanitaire (alors que les autorités de santé demandent que les employés qui le peuvent fassent du télétravail) ou lorsque cette crise sanitaire sera terminée?
Je vous remercie à l’avance,
threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Bonjour,
Voir ci-dessous notre réponse à votre question.
Question: Dans le cas d’un employé dont la ville de son employeur apparait comme lieu de travail sur son permis de travail peut-il effectuer du télétravail à partir de son domicile situé dans une autre ville sans contrevenir aux conditions énoncées à son permis? Existe-t-il une tolérance à ce niveau ou une demande de changement des conditions du permis de travail doit-elle plutôt être faite pour ajouter cet autre lieu de travail qui est son domicile?
Est-ce que la réponse est la même selon que l’on se situe en période de crise sanitaire (alors que les autorités de santé demandent que les employés qui le peuvent fassent du télétravail) ou lorsque cette crise sanitaire sera terminée?
Réponse: Il y a deux types de conditions qui entre en jeu dans le lieu de travail-celles imposées au travailleur temporaire sous la section 185 du Règlement sur l'immigration et la protection des réfugiés (RIPR) et celles imposées à l'employeur sous 209.3 du RIPR. Si le lieu de travail est imposé sur le permis de travail, le travailleur temporaire doit changer les conditions pour changer le lieu de travail.
Pour les travailleurs effectuant du télétravail de façon temporaire à partir de leur demeure au Canada à cause de la pandémie, il est recommandé que les employeurs soumettent une divulgation volontaire pour aviser IRCC de ce changement.
Dans le scénario où un employeur aimerait intégrer le télétravail de façon permanente après COVID, nous recommandons que l'employeur soumette une nouvelle offre d'emploi et que les travailleurs temporaires soumettent une demande pour changer leurs conditions de permis de travail.
Nous recommandons aussi que l'employeur inclue tout arrangement de télétravail dans toute nouvelle offre d'emploi. L'employeur doit également tenir à jour toute la documentation connexe et la présenter comme pièce justificative au moment de l'inspection.
Si l'employeur pense ne pas satisfaire aux conditions, il peut recourir au processus de divulgation volontaire.
Nous espérons que ces renseignements vous seront utiles.
Cordialement,
Représentants immigration (IRCC)

threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
My name is I am an RCIC I have a prospective client whose primary occupation is NOC 3234 — Paramedical occupations Skill Level B and whose foreign education is equivalent to the Canadian First professional degree in medicine. Could you please direct me with
regards to the following:
1) Do you accept ECA performed by MCC for applicants whose primary occupation is not NOC 3111 or NOC 3112? The IRCC website specifies that applicants under NOC 3111 or NOC 3112 must complete an ECA with Medical Council of Canada (MCC), however there is no explicit prohibition that applicants under other medical occupations cannot use MCC as an education assessment provider.
2)EE CRS: In this situation, will the person be awarded CRS points for “Master's degree, OR professional degree needed to practice in a licensed profession"? As per this IRCC web page tool, First professional degree in medicine is equivalent to Professional degree needed to practice in a licensed profession and is awarded 135 points (without a spouse). However, according to Ministerial Instructions respecting Express Entry, those points are awarded for education "the level of an entry-to-practice professional degree for an occupation listed in the National Occupational Classification matrix at Skill level A for which licensing by a provincial regulatory body is required" while the primary NOC of the person (NOC 3234) is in Skill Level B.
3) If the person doesn't qualify for 135 points as described above, how many points will they be awarded under CRS and which level of education, if not the "level of entry-to practice", shall we indicate in the EE profile?
4) How many points will the applicant be awarded under the Federal Skilled Worker score grid for education factor?
Thank you in advance for your clarifications.
Sincerely,
RCIC
Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant
Answer:
If the degree is considered an international medical degree than an ECA from MCC may be accepted. The Medical Council of Canada (MCC) is an ECA service provider organization –providing Educational Credential Assessments for immigration purposes (to IRCC), as well as for other credential recognition uses in the field of medicine. I'd invite you to visit MCC's ECAlanding page on their website, where they outline that they are able to provide
assessments only for International Medical Graduates (IMGs) for immigration purposes. As mentioned by IRCC website you pointed to, the occupations are those that fit the NOC 3111 or NOC 3112 definitions.
In order to be considered under “First professional degree or entry-to-practice professional degree" by IRCC (and to be awarded points accordingly), the occupation must be categorized as a Skill Level A occupation and one of the eight occupations currently considered under the definition – which are medicine, veterinary medicine, dentistry, podiatry, optometry and law. Once received, the ECAreport will identify the education credential awarded.
To determine points under the Federal Skilled Worker score grid for education factor please see the following IRCC web page tool as it outlines the equivalency outcomes under both CRS and FSWP factor points. Points will be awarded in accordance with 78(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR).
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Client may not be eligible for a PGWP if they have taken an unauthorized leave from their program of study and the IRCC officer finds that client has not met the conditions of their study permit. When an officer reviews a client's official documents from school confirming that they were not enrolled from a school or they were suspended from a school or study program, the client may be asked to leave Canada as they did not meet the study permit conditions. They might also wait 6 months before they can apply for new study permit. Not following the study permit conditions or studying in a way that it is not authorized, could also negatively affect the future applications that client would submit.
Question: If they are not eligible as a result of the above, are they eligible for the PGWP if this happened more than 6 months ago and they have since been a full time student?
Considering the overall situation if client enrolls in a new program, here are the requirements to be eligible for PGWP.
Client must have:
completed a study program At a designated learning institution That was at least 8 months long and That led to a degree, diploma or certificate
maintained full-time status as a student in Canada during each semester of their study permit, this doesn't include their final semester, which can be part-time or if they took an approved leave from their studies
graduated from one of the following:
a public post-secondary school, such as a college, trade/technical school, university or CEGEP (in Quebec)
a private post-secondary school (in Quebec) that operates under the same rules as public schools in Quebec a private secondary or post-secondary school (in Quebec) that offers qualifying programs of 900 hours or longer, that leads to a diplôme d’études professionnelles (DEP) or an attestation de spécialisation professionnelle (ASP) an ASP can be less than 900 hours if it's combined with a DEP a Canadian private school that can award degrees under provincial law (for example, Associate, Bachelor's, Master's
or Doctorate degree), but only if you're enrolled in a study program that leads to a degree as authorized by the province
Question: Finally, if the student stays in Canada but applies for visitor status and then continues studies as soon as the school allows them to enroll are they eligible for the PGWP?
After changing client's status to visitor, a student may resume their studies, using their previous study permit, as long as the study permit is valid.Students who submit the “Application to Change Conditions, Extend My Stay or Remain in Canada As a Student" form [IMM 5709] before the expiry date of the previous study permit hold implied status [R183(6)]. Under implied status, study permit holders may continue their studies under the same conditions as their previous study permit if they applied to extend their stay in Canada as a student. However, if they applied to extend their stay as a visitor, they may not pursue their studies when their current permit expires. Holding a visitor status client is not eligible for PGWP as PGWP eligibility is that client needs to be holding a valid study permit at the time of application.
Thank you kindly,

Can a refugee claimant continue to work while waiting to get their renewed work permit if they applied prior to the expiration?
Thanks
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
threads.answer:
Good day
Thank you for contacting us with your inquiry.
Question
Can a refugee claimant continue to work while waiting to get their renewed work perinit if they applied prior to the expiration?
Answer
Refugee claimants does not hold valid status and are simply applying for a work permit renewal under section R201 but not the extension of status under section R181.
The work perinit renewal application initiates the authorization to work without a permit under paragraph R186(u), but the application does not confer or extend status under subsection R183(5) as they have no status.
Therefore, a claimant who has submitted an application for a work permit extension may continue to work, without a work permit as per R186(u), until a decision is made on the application.

threads.subject: Postdocs holding Postdoc Association Positions -- REP-2021-0456
threads.question:
# Hello,
My name is, and I am a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant employed at the I am hoping you can provide us an official opinion on the following, which was recently brought up to us from the
There are 6 executive team positions available on the PDAC, and each executive is elected into the position for a 12month term, and receives an honorarium of $350 per month.
The question that has been brought up to us, is that there is a large international postdoctoral population here at the a majority of which are in possession of C44-LMIA exempt employer specific work permits. In the event that an international postdoctoral associate gets elected onto the executive team, are they legally allowed to perform the executive duties, and receive the honorarium, on their work permits? Being as these are elected positions, and only current postdocs are eligible to run, the honorarium and additional duties would not have been included on the employer portal submission for the work permits.
Please note the additional following details that were provided to us from the PDAC:
1. The PDAC Executive Team is composed of 6 positions
2. All individuals who fill the Executive Team positions must be current postdocs at the
3. Each position receives an honorarium of $350 per month, equating to $4,200 per annual term
4. The term of each position is 12 months, every position goes through another election after the year
5. There is no minimum time commitment required of the PDAC executive team positions. Each elected position dedicates to the PDAC the time that their postdoctoral position permits. On average, most positions commit around 1- 2hrs/week.
Based on the above, can you please provide us with an IRCC opinion to the question: In the event that an international postdoctoral associate gets elected onto the executive team, are they legally allowed to perform the executive duties, and
receive the honorarium, on their C-44 LMIA-exempt employer specific work permits?
We appreciate any guidance you're able to provide. Please let m know if you need any further information.
Kind regards,
Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Hello,
QuESTioN: In the event that an international postdoctoral associate gets elected onto the executive team, are they legally allowed to perform the executive duties, and receive the honorarium, on their work permits? Being as these are elected positions, and only current postdocs are eligible to run, the honorarium and additional duties would not have been included on the employer portal submission for the work permits.
RESPoNSE: The Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations require that the employer provide the foreign worker with employment in the same occupation as that set out in the offer of employment and with wages and working conditions that are substantially the same as, but not less favourable than, those in the same offer [R209.2(1)(a)(iii)]. In this situation, assuming that the foreign worker must agree to be nominated, the occupation and work duties would not be viewed as 'less favourable than' just the duties of the post-doctoral occupation. The employer could justify the variance in duties by stating that the foreign worker agreed to the nomination, received extra experience and an honorarium, so therefore the variance was not detrimental to the worker.
In the future, I would suggest that the employer could add a line to the offer of employment indicating 'may be elected to PDAC Executive Team' which would cover them for any future offers of employment.
For more information on 'Variance in duties' and how IRCC assesses them you can review the officer guidance publically available here: Assessing compliance conditions. Specifically, the section titled : Occupation, wages and working conditions

In the initial question you asked if an applicant could say their country of residence is Canada if they are on a short trip outside Canada. Our response is that if the client considers Canada as their main country of residence, then they may use that as their address. However, they must indicate that they are applying from outside Canada and submit the correct form. If a student is in Canada and planning to travel for vacation, we would advise they submit their application prior to travelling to make sure they have all the required documents to return to Canada. If a student is applying for an extension and requires a new temporary resident visa(TRV), then there would need to be a separate application submitted to obtain a TRV. However, if an applicant is leaving Canada for an extended time, we would advise they submit their application in the country they are residing to make sure they have all required documents to enter Canada.

Réponse : Les personnes qui présentent une demande de résidence permanente au Canada doivent mentionner les noms des membres de leur famille dans leur demande. Tous les membres de la famille doivent également faire l’objet d’un contrôle dans le cadre de la demande de résidence permanente afin de s’assurer qu’il n’existe aucune interdiction de territoire rendant le demandeur principal inadmissible à la résidence permanente, que les membres de sa famille l’accompagnent au Canada ou non. Cela vise les personnes suivantes : son époux/épouse ou conjoint(e) de fait, ses enfants à charge, les enfants à charge de son époux/épouse ou conjoint(e) de fait et les enfants à charge d’enfants à charge.
Si le/la conjoint(e) de fait est interdit(e) de territoire, la demande de résidence permanente pourrait également être refusée en raison de l’interdiction de territoire d’un membre de la famille même si celui--ci n’accompagne pas le demandeur principal, en vertu de l’article 42 de la Loi sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés (LiPR)/l’article 23 du Règlement sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés (RiPR). On recommande au/à la conjoint(e) de fait du demandeur principal, avant que ce dernier ne présente une demande de résidence permanente, de prendre des mesures afin de remédier à son interdiction de territoire.
En vertu de l’article 42 de la LiPR, une personne à qui l’on a accordé la résidence temporaire au Canada n’est pas interdite de territoire si son/sa conjoint(e) de fait est interdit(e) de territoire (pour des motifs autres que ceux mentionnés aux articles 34, 35 ou 37). Bien qu’un agent qui examine la demande de résidence permanente puisse déterminer que le demandeur principal n’est pas admissible à la résidence permanente au titre de l’article 42 de la LiPR et de l’article 23 du RIPR en raison du/de la conjoint(e) de fait interdit(e) de territoire qui l’accompagne, le demandeur principal ne perdrait pas son statut de résident temporaire au Canada.
Veuillez noter que les demandeurs sont tenus de répondre à toutes les questions aux fins de l’examen en toute honnêteté,
L'nmndion conformément au paragraphe 16(1) de la LIPR. Les demandes sont évaluées au cas par cas, en tenant compte de leurs circonstances particulières et des documents à l’appui dont dispose l’agent. Il incombe toujours au demandeur de fournir une
documentation suffisante pour convaincre un agent qu’il satisfait aux exigences.
Veuillez trouver ci-dessous les références aux dispositions législatives pertinentes : Inadmissibilité familiale 42 (1) Emportent, sauf pour le résident permanent ou une personne protégée, interdiction de territoire pour inadmissibilité familiale les faits suivants :
a) l’interdiction de territoire frappant tout membre de sa famille qui l’accompagne ou qui, dans les cas réglementaires, ne l’accompagne pas;
b) accompagner, pour un membre de sa famille, un interdit de territoire.
Note marginale: Exception
(2) Dans le cas où l’étranger visé au paragraphe (1) est résident temporaire ou dans le cas où il a présenté une demande pour obtenir le statut de résident temporaire ou une demande de séjour au Canada à titre de résident temporaire :
a) les faits visés à l’alinéa (1)a) emportent interdiction de territoire seulement si le membre de sa famille est interdit de territoire en raison d’un cas visé aux articles 34, 35 ou 37;
b) les faits visés à l’alinéa (1)b) emportent interdiction de territoire seulement si le membre de sa famille qu’il accompagne est interdit de territoire en raison d’un cas visé aux articles 34, 35 ou 37.

threads.question:
Dear IMMREP Officer,
I have a question with respect to CRS points for Express Entry for Intra-company transfer work permit holder.
A Foreign National (FN) has obtained an Intra-Company Transfer Work Permit under 205(a) (C-12) as a Managing Director (NOC 0). The Canadian corporation is wholly owned by a foreign corporate entity. The FN is the majority shareholder of that foreign corporation. The FN national is currently employed by the Canadian corporation as a Managing Director and is on their payroll.
For the purposes of applying for permanent residency under Express Entry in either CEC or FSW category:
1) Is the FN considered to be engaged in 'self-employment' or 'Self-employed'? (what definition of self-employment is used?)
2) After one year of Canadian work experience, is the FN eligible for the 200 CRS points for a qualifying offer of arranged employment? (per. 29(2)(a)(iïi Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Express Entry System )
3) After acquiring one year of Canadian work experience and subject to attaining sufficient CRS points to obtain ITA, is the FN eligible to apply under either Federal Skilled Working class or Canadian Experience Class?
Thanks,
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: A Foreign National (FN) has obtained an Intra-Company Transfer Work Permit under 205(a) (C-12) as a Managing Director (NOC 0). The Canadian corporation is wholly owned by a foreign corporate entity. The FN is the majority shareholder of that foreign corporation. The FN national is currently employed by the Canadian corporation as a Managing Director and is on their payroll. For the purposes of applying for permanent residency under Express Entry in either CEC or FSW category: Is the FN considered to be engaged in 'self-employment' or 'Self-employed'? (what definition of self-employment is used?)
Answer: Program requirements vary between Express Entry programs. For the Canadian Experience Class, the onus is on the applicant to provide supporting documents and satisfy the officer that they meet all program requirements and prove they are not self-employed. The CEC requires that applicants demonstrate they acquired skilled work experience in Canada through authorized employment by a third party. For your information, our internal guidance to determine whether an applicant under CEC was an employee or a self-employed individual during their period of qualifying work experience can be found on our website. Please note that each application under the CEC will be considered on its own merits, with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision. For the Federal Skilled Worker program, there is no such restrictions on self-employment, but applicants must continue to meet all program requirements, as per section 75 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations.
Note: If the prospective applicant is not sure of their employment status, they may choose to request a ruling from the
CRA to have their status determined. Such a ruling will state whether, in the view of the CRA, a worker is an employee or self-employed. The link provided also contains indicators which show whether someone is an employee or self-employed. It should be noted that individuals who hold substantial ownership and/or exercise management control of a business for which they are also employed are generally considered to be self-employed. While the CRA ruling on an applicant's employment status will be given due consideration, such a ruling will not constitute conclusive evidence. The final decision as to the employment status of the applicant rests with the Officer. Question: After one year of Canadian work experience, is the FN eligible for the 200 CRS points for a qualifying offer of arranged employment? threads.subject: Questions-Dependents of diplomatic agents -- REP-2021-0683
threads.question:
Good afternoon, Please see below our response to this request:
1. Can a dependent of a diplomatic agent hold both a study permit and diplomatic visa?
Yes, but there are many scenarios to this question depending on if the diplomatic dependent is under the age of 19 or over but less than 25 years.
All persons coming to Canada on posting, including their family members, must be in possession of diplomatic or official visas.
Dependent children under 19 years of age who are considered members of the family forming part of the household will be issued an acceptance counterfoil by the Office of Protocol. They do not require a study permit. Children from 19 to 24 years of
age are only issued an acceptance counterfoil if they are registered as full-time students.
Foreign representatives’ dependent children in Canada who are 25 years of age or older may be considered for an official acceptance only in exceptional circumstances.
See the Office of Protocol policy on the accreditation of immediate family members of foreign representatives.
2. If they can hold both and thus obtain both, can they work on the basis of their study permit without obtaining prior authorization from the Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade (DFAIT)?
Children of foreign representatives shall not undertake employment on university or college campus, nor shall they engage in off- campus gainful occupation, unless authorized in writing by the Office of Protocol. The Office of Protocol will, upon official request from the diplomatic mission issue a work authorization provided that: • the applicant is accredited;
- there exists a Reciprocal Employment Agreements and Arrangements (REA) between Canada and the sending state concerned;
- the applicant submits a copy of a valid work offer, only in the case of countries that impose such a condition on Canadians;
- the applicant does not intend to operate a sole proprietorship or with someone else as a partnership (see 7.3);
- it is understood that the person's civil and administrative immunities with respect to all matters arising out of employment is
and Cizenship Canedaot Cioyenneté Canada
waived by the sending State, the international organization or the office.
3. If they can hold both and thus obtain both, must they first request a letter of no objection from the Office of Protocol of DFAIT in order to apply for a post-graduate work permit after completing their program of studies?
Work authorizations issued by the Department ofForeign Affairs and International Trade (DFAIT) pursuant to this policy cannot be used for the purpose of work under post graduate work permit program of Citizenship and Immigration Canada. Missions must first request a letter of no objection from the Office of Protocol ofDFAIT in this regard to enable the individual to apply for
a postgraduate work permit with IRCC.
Thank you kindly,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: PR card renewals by PRs outside of Canada w/o domestic address -- REP-2020-2811
threads.question:
Hello,
Thank you for your inquiry.
A residential address in Canada is required when a PR is completing an application for a PR card renewal. A PR card will not be mailed to a third party address. If a third party address is provided on the application form, processing will be delayed until a residential address is provided. The PR card will only be sent to the residential address in Canada provided by the client or a post office (PO) box, if this is the client's residential mailing address.
Since an application for a PR card renewal must be made from within Canada, the client will need to return to Canada in order to complete and submit their application. The residential mailing address where the client will be residing while they are in Canada would be address to provide on their application form.
If the clients PR card is expired, the client will need to apply for a PRTD to return to Canada in order to apply for a PR card renewal.
For more information, please follow the link below: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-) 5445-applying-permanent-resident-card-card-first-application-replacement-renewal-change-gender-identifier.html

There are 2 scenarios for assessing the validity of police certificates:
1. If you live in the country currently, then the police certificate must be issued within 6 months of filing the case -ie. within the last six months while you're still living there.
2. If you previously lived in the country, then the police certificate must be issued after the last time your stayed there for 6 months or more in a row. We need clarification on this.
a. Does this mean: that you have to have physically left the country in order to apply for the police certificate? That would be difficult as that no person could ever apply for a police certificate while physically in the country, even if they leave the country the week after.
b. Or, does this mean that IRCC applies the same logic as they do for the test for police certificates from your current country–that the police certificate must be issued within six months of leaving the country (so you that you're not in the country for 6 months or more without having had a police certificate). The way the 6 months is counted is that from the time you get your police certificate, you cannot remain in the country to trigger the police certificate requirement again. For example, if you obtain a police certificate in May 2017 from country X, then leave country X in August 2017–meaning you were in the country 3 months -you would not trigger a new police certificate requirement because you would not in the country for a new ‘six months in a row'.
This would then enable certain applicants to re-use the police certificate for permanent residence that applicants use to get their work permits, as long as the applicant left their country within 6 months of issuance of the police certificate.
Your assistance is greatly appreciated. Thank you.
Kind regards,

of the Access to Information Act de la Loi sur l'acces a l'information

L'information divulguée en vertu de la toi sur Faccés à Tinfomation
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's (IRCC) Immigration Representatives mailbox.
In response to your first question, you are correct. Applicants are requested to submit a police certificate for countries they have resided for more than 6 months since the age of 18 along with their application for permanent residence. Furthermore, applicants may request a police certificate while living in their current country of residence, as long as they are still residing in this country at the time of submitting their application.
This being said, police certificate requirements may vary according to each line of business. We recommend reviewing the specific requirements for each line of business, as you have done so for Police certificates for Express Entry applications-Canada.ca. As you may have noticed, Express Entry requirements state that the police certificate for the country where you currently live must be issued no more than 6 months before the date you submit your application and must not be expired.
Also of note for Express Entry applications, if your client is invited to apply, they have 90 days to submit their application for permanent residence. If they do not have all their police certificates by the 90-day deadline, they have 2 options:
Option 1: Decline your invitation to apply
Their profile will go back in the pool and they may be invited to apply again.
Option 2: Prove you applied for the police certificate In very rare cases, IRCC may accept both a letter of explanation and proof that shows your client made your best effort to get a police certificate on time.
With regard to your question 2(b), it would appear that your client's police certificate does not cover the entire period (more than six months in a row until August 2017) they resided in country X. We suggest requesting a new police certificate from the country's authorities which covers the period your client resided in country X for more than 6 months in a row, thus until August 2017.
As with any case, the officer reviewing the file may require further documentation in order to be satisfied that the applicant is not criminally inadmissible.
We trust that this information will be useful to you.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Good day,
I assisted clients to present PR applications under the TR to PR Pathway, under the French Speaking International Graduates Stram (Diplômés étrangers d’expression française).
It has been reported by my clients that under the portal, there is a very important mistake, which induced many people in error:

Cioyenneté Canada

threads.answer:

Question: I need to clarify the minimum requirements under CEC." Have at least 1 year of skilled work experience in Canada, in the last 3 years before you apply." If the candidate is not currently working, does the 3-year time frame start from the date of ITA or the date of AOR? For example. Answer: For the Canadian Experience Class (CEC), applicants must have acquired in Canada, within the three years before the date on which their application for permanent residence (e-APR) is made, at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work experience, as per R87.1(2)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: Could you please clarify whether someone working on a valid open work permit in Canada for a foreign company can use that work experience to qualify under CEC if:
- The worker was employed remotely through the foreign company and paid through the foreign company
- The employee didn't need the work permit to work in Canada, though held one at the time. Answer: Canadian work experience is work experience that is acquired by a foreign national in Canada as per 87.1(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. The applicant must physically be in Canada, and participating in the Canadian Labour market. The applicant also must have temporary status during the qualifying periods of work experience acquired in Canada. If the applicant “didn't need the work permit to work in Canada” then this does not constitute Canadian work experience. Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements. We trust that this information will assist you. threads.subject: Student's work eligibility during a scheduled break prior to their final part-time semester -- REP-2021-0575
threads.question:
Hello,
A student may work full-time if they are on a scheduled break; such as winter and summer holidays, or a fall or spring reading week. The student must be a full-time student both before and after the break to work full-time. Part-time student can work off campus only if:
- you meet all of the requirements above and
- you're only studying part-time, instead of full-time, because: o you're in the last semester of your study program and you don't need a full course load to complete your program and o you were a full-time student in your program in Canada, up until your last semester
More information can be found at this link: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html#pt](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html#pt)

threads.subject: Work permit exemption for health care studies (dental assistants from foreign schools) -- REP-2021-0645
threads.question:
Dear ImmReps,
I am a lawyer in Ontario. I have a question with respect to the work permit exemption under 186(P) of the IRPR. The instruction
guide on the IRCC webpage says the following:
Medical teaching institutions are identified in the IRPR as employers for medical students under paragraph R186(p). However, workplaces such as private clinics are also permitted if they are providing human health care training.
Health care fields include the following:
- medicine (including dentistry)
- occupational and physical therapy
- medical technology
- nursing
- other professions in human health care that are regulated by provincial or territorial governments
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
I would like some clarification if dental assistants students from foreign jurisdictions coming for training to Canada meet this exemption. Dental assisting is not an MD program. In fact, is the MD program a requirement for this exemption, or not? If it is, why is there an additional requirement for the field to be regulated. Aren't all MD progessions regulated in Canada? In addition, the other helthcare programs that are identified by the Guide are nursing and physical therapy-neither one of them are MD programs. Not every province in Canada regulates dental assistants, so the requirement that the field will be regulated is unclear-is this a mandatory requirement, or not.
Looking forward to your clarification on the mandatory requirements.
Sincerely,
threads.answer:
Hello, Dental assistant students are covered by R186(p), provided that their employer provides educational or practical training to
the student. Dental care is considered a medical field and as such, the work they are performing would fall under this categorization.
Being in an MD program is not a mandatory requirement for R186. It should also be noted that once the MD (or the initial degree) is obtained, the subject is no longer considered to be a 'student' and would not fall within this work without a permit category.
There is no specific requirement that the field of study be regulated. The language in the instruction is that the student must "have written approval from the body in Canada that regulates that field." Therefore, logically, if there is no regulatory body for the health care field then no written approval is needed for that specific province and occupation.
Thank you kindly,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Permis d etudes et de stage -- REP-2021-0784
threads.question:
Bonjour,
Les étudiants qui se trouvent déjà au Canada et qui ont demandé un permis de travail – stage coop peuvent commencer leur stage coop grâce à leur autorisation du programme à travailler sur le campus et hors campus, à condition de respecter tous les critères d’admissibilité.
Les étudiants peuvent travailler à temps plein sur le campus de l’université ou du collège qu’ils fréquentent à temps plein conformément au [R186f)]. Dans le cadre de l’autorisation du programme de travail hors campus [R186v)], ils peuvent travailler jusqu’à 20 heures par semaine pendant un trimestre ou un semestre d’études, ce qui comprend à la fois les heures prévues au stage coop et les heures consacrées à leur emploi rémunéré normal (s’ils en ont un). Ils peuvent également travailler à temps plein pendant les congés prévus au calendrier d’études.
Toutefois, si la demande de stage coop est refusée, l’étudiant doit cesser de travailler immédiatement.
Si vous avez d’autres questions, n’hésitez pas à nous recontacter.
Cordialement,
Représentants immigration (IRCC)

threads.subject: Question regarding Extension of public policy allowing visitors to apply for work permits inside Canada -- REP- 2021-0462
threads.question:
Hello,
Response : As per paragraph R183(5) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, if a temporary resident has applied for an extension of the period authorized of their stay and a decision has not been made by the end of the period authorized for their stay, the period is extended. The temporary resident has a valid status until a decision has been made, if the application is refused (as per paragraph R183(5)(a)), or until the end of the new period authorized for their stay, if the application is allowed (as
per paragraph R183(5)(b)). For more information visit this webpage. Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Question concernant congé d'études -- REP-2020-2835
threads.question:
Bonjour,
Selon nos instructions relatives à l’exécution du programme, un étudiant qui désire prendre un congé de leurs études, et désire rester au Canada durant cette période, peut demander une autorisation de leur établissement d’étude désignée et prendre jusqu’à 150 jours consécutifs de congé. On considère qu’un étudiant en congé autorisé qui commence ou reprend ses études dans les 150 jours qui suivent la date de début du congé (c'est-à-dire la date à laquelle l’établissement lui a accordé un congé) poursuit activement ses études pendant son congé. Si l’étudiant a l’intention de quitter le Canada durant cette période, ce règlement ne s’applique pas et l’étudiant pourrait prendre congé sans autorisation.
Dans le cas d’un étudiant ayant pris plusieurs périodes de congé au Canada pendant son programme d’études, l’agent doit tenir compte des raisons invoquées par l’étudiant. Si les périodes de congé ne semblent pas appuyer la réalisation de progrès raisonnables vers la réussite du cours ou du programme dans le délai prévu dans le cadre du cours ou du programme, l’agent peut conclure que le titulaire du permis d’études n’a pas respecté la condition de poursuite active de son cours ou de son programme d’études.
Pour plus de renseignements, veuillez visiter notre site web.
Cordialement,
La boîte aux lettres des représentants de l'immigration
