threads.question:
Hello, Scenario: Foreign national in Canada on PGWP (Post-Graduation Work Permit) which is expiring. FN marries a Canadian and is
preparing to submit a sponsorship and spousal OWP application. However, cannot submit before expiry of PGWP. So FN applies for visitor extension (IMM5708) before expiry of PGWP. Following that, FN/Canadian spouse submit sponsorship and
spousal OWP extension IMM5710).
Response to Scenario: Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case-specific advice. Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements. For case-specific resources and assistance, see the links below.
Question #1: If visitor extension is granted before the WP is processed, will the WP application be treated as an application to extend that visitor status and granted?
Answer #1: If the FN submits form IMM5708, the application to change conditions, extend stay or remain in Canada as a visitor and this change is approved, the OWP application will be processed under their current status. The approval of form IMM5708 does not guarantee the approval of the work permit.
Question #2: If visitor extension is not granted before the WP is processed, will the WP be processed as priority instead of the visitor extension?
Answer #2: The WP will not be processed as priority if the visitor extension is not granted as this circumstance does not fall under one of the streams for priority processing.
Question #3: What, if anything, should the applicant do to alert IRCC to the two interplaying applications, given that
ultimately what the FN wants is to get a spousal OWP?
Answer #3: The applicant does not need to take additional steps to alert IRCC of the two applications.

threads.answer: Hello, Question: Can you please clarify if the degree listed for each occupation on the NAFTA professionals list needs to be that exact degree to qualify. Example: For example, a client holding a Masters in Social Work (but not bachelors) can qualify as a social worker in Ontario, but does not hold a bachelor's degree in Social work, could you please let us know if officers have any discretion when it comes to the education requirements? Answer: Appendix 2 of CUSMA is the comprehensive list of 63 occupations, and their individual minimum education requirements. As explained in our online guidance, this Appendix is a complete list and cannot be interpreted. Additionally, as noted in subsection 3.2 "The Minimum Education Requirements and Alternative Credentials indicated for each profession are minimum criteria for entry and do not necessarily reflect the educational requirements, accreditation or licensing necessary to practice a profession in Canada." Therefore, while an individual may be able to enter based on their education level, this does not guarantee their right to work. Ultimately, it is the onus of the applicant to provide enough evidence to satisfy the officer that the applicant qualifies for their desired position. We trust you will find this information useful and thank you for your patience. Regards, The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Clarification of Mandatory Hotel Stay Exemption -- REP-2021-0585
threads.question:
Hello,
If the temporary foreign worker falls within one of the exempted occupations (such as 0821-Agricultural Managers), they are exempted from the Mandatory Hotel Stay. In that case, the worker needs to have no symptoms of COVID-19, has to travel to the final place of quarantine in a private vehicle and has to travel only with those who arrived on the same flight. If all these criteria are met, then the temporary foreign worker is exempted from the Mandatory Hotel Stay. For more information visit this website.

threads.subject: Query Regarding BO WP eligibility for an Express Entry Applicant working on a Closed Work Permit -- REP- 2021-0660
threads.question:
nmigration, Réfugiés
Dear Imm Rep,
Request your inputs on this scenario of Bridging Open Work Permit,
An applicant who is working on an LMIA based Closed Work Permit with an Employer in Canada, got an ITA and submitted his EAPR. His Employer specific work permit is expiring soon. Our queries are :
1. Since he submitted his EAPR, is he Eligible to apply for BOWP ?
2. If he is eligible for BOWP and gets his BOWP, Can he start working with any Employer or he will have to keep working with the same employer who gave him LMIA and work permit for his Express Entry.
3. If he is not eligible for BOWP, does he need a fresh LMIA and work permit to have a valid status and work authorization in Canada ?
Request your opinion on these 3 points.
Thanks a lot for your kind consideration and valuable time,
Best Wishes,
et Ciloyenneé Canada
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: An applicant who is working on an LMIA based Closed Work Permit with an Employer in Canada, got an ITA and submitted his EAPR. His Employer specific work permit is expiring soon. Since he submitted his EAPR, is he Eligible to apply for BOWP?
Answer: Yes, if the applicant applied for Express Entry, they would be eligible to apply for a BOWP if they meet the criteria below (and found on our website): live in Canada (Quebec not included) have a valid work permit that expires in 4 months or less be the principal applicant on their permanent residence application have submitted a complete application for permanent residence and passed the completeness check have the acknowledgement of receipt letter (we send this letter to their account after receiving their permanent residence application)
Question: If he is eligible for BOWP and gets his BOWP, can he start working with any Employer or he will have to keep working with the same employer who gave him LMIA and work permit for his Express Entry.
Answer: Applicants may be able to change their employers after they secure a BOWP, as long as the applicant remains eligible to work in Canada. For more information on extending or changing the conditions of your work permit, please refer to our website.
Question: If he is not eligible for BOWP, does he need a fresh LMIA and work permit to have a valid status and work authorization in Canada?
Answer: Yes, a work permit or authorization to work without a permit is required in order for a foreign national to be allowed to work in Canada. For more information on extending or changing the conditions of your work permit, please refer to our website.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: After obtaining a PCC from one country, if one visits back again to the same country for short trip (less than 6 months), would he require to obtain and submit a fresh new PCC after his last visit? Will his trip make the previously obtained PCC invalid, even the trip is less than 6 months?
Answer: No, applicants who are 18 years or older must submit a police certificate for every country they've stayed in during the last years for 6 months or more in a row. Additional information on required police certificate can be found on our website.
Question: Can an EE -CEC candidate, residing in Canada but on a visit to his home country, submit the PR application online (EE) from his home country while on a visit to meet the application deadline? Or he must get back to Canada and then apply?
Answer: The applicant does not need to be in Canada to apply. Applicants do not have to be employed at the time of application under CEC, but they must have had temporary status during the qualifying period of work experience acquired in Canada.
Question: If someone created an EE profile with a dummy ECA or IELTS details, and gets an ITA, can he update the ECA or IELTS details post ITA during the e-APR, if his score stays higher than the cut-off score and provide letter of explanation? Would this be misrepresentation?
Answer: Yes, submitting false or altered documents is considered misrepresentation. Do not submit false or altered documents. Language test results must be less than two years old when you submit your application for permanent residence. More information on language test results can be found on our website.
Question: Can one make his “non-accompanying" spouse to “accompanying” post ITA at the time of e-APR if the spouse is temporary living in Canada with the applicant? Will this cause recalculation of points?
Answer: Yes, family members can be added to the application at any time during the process, but must be added prior to obtaining permanent resident status. All family members must be examined as part of the electronic application for permanent residence, whether they are accompanying the principal applicant or not. Applicants are instructed to inform IRCC of any changes to their family composition. If your situation changes, you should re-calculate your score before applying online for permanent residence. If your re-calculated score is less than the lowest score in your round of invitations, you should decline the invitation.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Postdoctoral fellow and visiting professor-Canadian Work Experience -- REP-2021-0437
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to ’s Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
My questions are:
1- Does time spent in Canada as a visiting scholar or professor count towards Canadian work experience for Express Entry? This was time spent working in Canada with a temporary work permit, but the person is paid by home university.
2- Does time spent in Canada as a postdoctoral fellow count towards Canadian work experience for Express Entry? This was time spent working in Canada with a temporary work permit, and the person is paid by the Canadian university.
3- Given that a postdoctoral fellow has been offered a contract extension to the second year, is it considered a valid job offer for Express Entry that is worth 50 CRS points?
Answer:
1- Please note that we do not respond to case specific questions. Based on the information provided however, this experience may constitute Canadian work experience. To apply for permanent residence under the Canadian Experience Class, your skilled work experience must:
- be in a job classified as skill type 0, or skill level A or B according to the 2016 National Occupational Classification,
- amount to at least one year of full-time (or an equal amount in part-time) in the previous three years,
- have been with an employer in Canada (self-employment does not count),
- be gained with the proper legal authorization (for example, as a documented worker with a valid work permit), and
- not be gained while you were studying on a student permit.
The experience you describe as a fellow in Canada on a temporary work permit may be counted as work experience, and not study, provided it meets the definition of work pursuant to Section 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, which states: despite the definition work in section 2, for the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. Please note that to be considered work, the applicant must have been paid wages or commission. A stipend or allowance, where the primary purpose is to cover expenses, would not generally be considered wages. The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer that there was the payment of wages and that all other requirements were met.
2- The experience you describe as a fellow in Canada on a temporary work permit may be counted as work experience, and not study, provided it meets the definition of work pursuant to Section 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, which states: despite the definition of work in section 2, for the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. Please note that to be considered work, the application must have been paid wages or commission. A stipend or allowance, where the primary purpose is to cover expenses, would not generally be considered wages. The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer that there was a payment of wages and that all other requirements were met. 3- Your job offer must:
- be recent (usually less than 1 year old) (You can't use the same job offer letter that you used to get your work permit.)
- be in writing
- not be from an embassy, high commission or consulate in Canada
- set out details of the job they're offering you, such as
- your pay and deductions
- your job duties conditions of employment, like your hours of work

threads.subject: AIPP Work Permit Extension-Expired Language-PR Application Already in Processing -- REP-2021-0697
threads.question:
Hello,
I am a lawyer and have a question regarding the language test requirements for applicants applying for Atlantic Immigration Pilot Program (“AIPP”) based work permit extensions.
IRCC's guidance and document checklist for AlPP work permits indicates that applicants must submit copies of valid language test results as part of their work permit applications. Specifically, these language test results must be less than 2 years old at the time of submission of the work permit.
Many applicants who submitted AIPP PR applications have been waiting for 10 months to over 1 year for their applications to be approved due to the COViD processing backlog. This has resulted in these applicants needing to apply for AlPP-based work permits to ensure that they remain in status until their PR application can be approved. Unfortunately, due to the lengthy processing time for the PR applications, many applicants have language test results that are now expired (over 2 years old) despite being valid at the time of submitting the AlPP PR application.
I am seeking clarification whether an applicant who has already submitted their AlPP PR residence application (and it is in processing) can rely on their now expired language for the AlPP work permit application?
While I understand that the guidance indicates that the language test results must be valid at the time of the work permit application, it seems illogical that an applicant whose PR application has been in processing for well over the stated processing times must now redo a language test simply to extend their work permit in Canada despite having valid ianguage test results at the time of submitting the PR application. I understand that the purpose of including the valid language test results with the AIPP work permit application is to ensure that an applicant actually qualifies for the AlPP PR program. This is seemingly not applicable if the applicant's AlPP PR application is already in processing as it is
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
clear that they met these basic requirements at the time of submitting the PR application and they are simply seeking to extend their status while awaiting their AlPP applications to be processed.
As you are likely well aware, language tests are very difficult to schedule due to COVID-19 and the recent surge of individuals requesting language tests due to IRCC's new TR to PR applications. Additionally, these language test results can be very expensive. As such, I am hopeful that IRCC would accept expired language test results for the AIPP work permit if it can be demonstrated that the results were valid at the time the AlPP PR application was received by
IRCC.
Thank you,

Bonjour,
Voir ci-dessous notre réponse à votre question.
Question: Un employeur, immatriculé au Canada et dont toutes les activités et le siège social se trouvent au Canada, prévoit signer un contrat de travail avec un étranger résidant hors du Canada qui n’est ni citoyen canadien, ni un résident permanent et n’a aucun statut au Canada afin qu'il exécute intégralement son travail à distance depuis l’étranger (en télétravail).
Serait-il possible de nous indiquer les conséquences sur le plan du droit de l’immigration d’un tel travail à distance tant au niveau du futur employé que de l’employeur dans l’éventualité où le travailleur ne viendra jamais au Canada pendant la durée de son contrat ?
Si le travailleur devait se rendre au Canada de manière ponctuelle pour une rencontre annuelle, quels seraient les documents d’immigration dont l’employé et/ou l’employeur auraient besoin?
Réponse: La première disposition pertinente pour le travail au Canada est le paragraphe 30 (1) de la Loi sur l'immigration et la protection des réfugiés (LiPR), qui stipule ce qui suit : L'étranger ne peut exercer un emploi au Canada ou y étudier que sous le régime de la présente loi.
L'interprétation de cette clause signifie que la LiPR et ses dispositions ne s'appliquent pas aux situations de travail à l'extérieur du pays; ainsi, même si le travail effectué répond à la définition de travail, il n'est pas pertinent puisque la LiPR ne s'applique pas au travail effectué à l'extérieur de nos frontières.
Si le travailleur devait se rendre au Canada de manière ponctuelle pour une rencontre annuelle, le travailleur pourrait être autorisé à travailler sans permis de travail en vertu du R186.
Pour de plus amples informations, veuillez consulter les sites suivants: Programme des travailleurs étrangers temporaires et Programme de mobilité international: Définition du terme "travail" Programme de mobilité internationale : Autorisation de travailler sans permis de travail dispense de permis de travail de courte durée (de 15 ou de 30 jours)
Nous espérons que ces renseignements vous seront utiles.

threads.subject: Professional Employer Organization and ICTs --REP-2021-0980
threads.question:
Dear ImmReps Officer;
I am seeking clarification on how IRCC treats/views Professional Employer Organizations in Canada.
For the purpose of the Offer of Employment filed with IRCC, should the employer be the Professional Employer Organization in Canada or the company receiving services in Canada?
If an employee who works for a company outside of Canada (but is paid by a Professional Employer Organization) is transferred to Canada to work for the company inside Canada (but be paid by the Professional Employer Organization) in Canada, for IRCC purposes, is the employee being transferred to the Canadian company or the Professional Employer Organization in Canada?
Employer A in US wants to transfer Bob to Employer B in Canada. However, Bob will be paid by a Professional Employer Organization in Canada.
Employer B previously employed people and previously had physical offices in Canada. All employees in Canada are now paid by the Professional Employer Organization and Employer B has given up their physical office because of COVID. Employer B has had a company in Canada for 5+ years. Employer B has no management structure in Canada, all of the management structure comes from Employer A.
Employer A also uses the same Professional Employer Organization in the United States. Bob is also paid by the Professional Employer Organization in the US.
Can Bob be transferred as an ICT under specialized knowledge for Employer B?
Can Bob be transferred as an ICT under specialized knowledge for the Professional Employer Organization?
Which employer (Employer B or the Professional Employer Organization) files the Offer of Employment?
Thank you,
Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Hello,
It should be noted any employer submitting an Offer of employment in the Employer Portal must meet the requirements of a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) exemption category. A Professional Employer Organization that contracts out their staff to other employers would not generally meet any existing LMIA exemptions for the contracted staff.
QUESTION 1: For the purpose of the Offer of Employment filed with IRCC, should the employer be the Professional Employer Organization in Canada or the company receiving services in Canada?
RESPONSE 1: You may review the instructions and information found in the Employer Portal enrollment guide for
information on 'Who needs to complete an offer of employment.'
If two Canadian companies are involved in the process of hiring a temporary foreign worker, the employer of record will be the one to submit to the offer of employer. The employer of record is the company that will ensure both employers are following the conditions of employing a temporary foreign worker. Find out more about these conditions and your responsibilities as an employer.
In all cases, the employer of record must be involved in hiring the temporary worker. This can include setting up the details of the job they will do and overseeing their work.
Therefore, if the Professional Employer Organization is taking on the role of employer of record, they can submit the offer of employment with the work location as the Canadian company. It must be noted in the Offer of employment how that situation meets a LMIA exemption category. In addition, please see the instructions in the Employer Portal User Guide on how
to enter wages-Wage and benefits form.
QUESTION 2: If an employee who works for a company outside of Canada (but is paid by a Professional Employer Organization) is transferred to Canada to work for the company inside Canada (but be paid by the Professional Employer Organization) in Canada, for IRCC purposes, is the employee being transferred to the Canadian company or the Professional
Employer Organization in Canada?

Good day,
If the student does not meet the below eligibility reguirements, they will not be eligible to apply for a PGWP.
To obtain a post-graduation work permit, the applicant must currently hold valid temporary status or have left Canada. They must have graduated from an eligible designated learning institution (DLl). They must also submit clear evidence that they meet all of the following criteria: ●They have completed an academic, vocational or professional training program at an eligible institution in Canada that is at least 8 months in duration leading to a degree, diploma or certificate.
- They have maintained full-time student status in Canada during each academic session of the program or programs of study they have completed and submitted as part of their post-graduation work permit application. Exceptions can be made only for the following: 0 leave from studies 0 final academic session They have received a transcript and an official letter from the eligible DLl confirming that they have met the requirements to complete their program of study.
Please be advised that any leave taken from a program of studies in Canada should not exceed 150 days from the date the leave commenced and must be authorized by their DLI.
The student can work full-time until we make a decision on their PGWP if:
had a valid study permit when they submitted their application,
•completed their study program, AND
were eligible to work off campus without a work permit while studying and they didn't work more hours than they
were allowed to.
If these conditions apply, they will need to prove to an employer that they are eligible to work, they should provide them with a copy of all the required documents.
If these conditions don't apply, the student must wait until their work permit arrives to begin working. It's illegal to work in Canada without authorization.
For more information, please visit our website: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/post-graduation-work-permit-program.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/post-graduation-work-permit-program.html)

threads.subject: question about protected person's ability to return to country of nationality for family emergency REP-2021-0953
threads.question:
Dear Immigration Representatives,
I am an immigration lawyer working at a Can you please advise whether the Department would issue a Refugee Travel Document, to a protected person in Canada, that would be valid to return to the country of nationality (i.e., the country against which the refugee protection had been granted)? The reason for travel would be to pay the last visit to a terminally ill parent who is in no position to re-unite with the
protected person in a third country.
Thank you in advance for your answer.
Iam a full member in good standing with the Law Society of Alberta, member ID #
Yours truly,
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for your enquiry about a Refugee Travel Document for your client and wish to inform you that according to www.canada.ca : "Convention refugees and protected persons can use a Refugee Travel Document (RTD), issued by the Passport Canada, in order to exit and re-enter Canada. A protected person who is not a permanent resident and who intends to travel outside Canada must obtain an RTD from the Passport Office before leaving Canada by submitting an Adult Travel Document Application (PPTC 190) or a Child Travel Document Application (PPTC 192).
The application must be accompanied by:
- a letter from the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB);
- a confirmation of permanent residence; or a Verification of Status (VOS) document.
The RTD is valid for travel to all countries except the country of persecution. Travellers must return to Canada prior to the expiry date indicated on the RTD and, at that time, they should have in their possession both the RTD and the protected person status document.
If a traveller is unable to produce a RTD due to the loss or theft of the document while outside Canada, the officer may issue a temporary resident permit in order to allow re-entry into Canada. Prior to issuing a permit, officers should question the applicant regarding the loss or theft of the RTD and be satisfied that the circumstances are genuine."
In the case of the client, referred to in the email below, and their wish to return to the country of persecution it does not appear that they would qualify for an RTD. Suggest contacting Passport Canada if further details/assistance is required.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Question on APR portal -- REP-2021-0989
threads.question:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a new RCIC and I am signing up on the APR portal.
I do not wish to pay any government fees on behalf of my clients, nor do I wish to have any refunds of government fees go to me instead ofmy clients.
How do I go about keeping all government fees payable, and all refunds returned directly to the client?
Thank you,
threads.answer:
Dear
Thank you for your enquiry.
The decision as to who pays the government fees is a decision made between a consultant and their client, and would be stated in the client agreement. threads.subject: Question on validity of custodianship declaration, certifications -- REP-2021-0295
threads.question:
Dear Sir / Madam:
1. When the custodianship declaration is signed and notarized, and then the admission is deferred for a year, is it allowed to use the same (last year's) notarized declaration to apply for a study permit, providing there is no change in information declared? The school that deferred admission already accepted the declaration for the initial admission and does not require an updated one.
2. Can signatures on a custodianship declaration be certified by a commissioner of oaths and affidavits, or does only notary public have a right to do it?
3. In general, is there a validity period of a notarized declaration or a similar declaration (statutory declaration of support, for instance) for the purpose of an immigration (study permit, in this case) application, if the declared information is unchanged?
Thank you for clarifying the answers to these three questions.
Respectfully / Cordialement,
threads.answer:
Hello,
1. When the custodianship declaration is signed and notarized, and then the admission is deferred for a year, is it allowed to use the same (last year's) notarized declaration to apply for a study permit, providing there is no change in information declared? The school that deferred admission already accepted the declaration for the initial admission and does not require an updated one.
The most up-to-date custodian form must be provided with a study permit application to IRCC by their parent(s) or the appointed paid immigration representative for a minor student at the time of application. If application is still in process, a new custodian form can be submitted to IRCC via web form.
To protect and safeguard the safety and wellbeing of the minor while studying in Canada, officers must be satisfied that adequate arrangements are in place for the care and support of the minor student. Officer may request additional information such as a new notarized custodian form is required.
2. Can signatures on a custodianship declaration be certified by a commissioner of oaths and affidavits, or does only notary public have a right to do it?
Outside of Canada, signatures on a custodianship declaration must be certified by a notary public or a person authorized to certify in that country.
3. In general, is there a validity period of a notarized declaration or a similar declaration (statutory declaration of support, for instance) for the purpose of an immigration (study permit, in this case) application, if the declared information is unchanged?
IRCC does not specify the validity period for a custodianship. As previously mentioned, the most up-to-date custodian form must be provided with a study permit application in order to protect the well-being of the minor while in Canada. Officers must be satisfied that the care and support of the minor is adequately arranged by the parents or legal guardians.
A couple of examples of why a recent document is required:
- Custody can be changed without the original custody form being reclaimed and destroyed.
- A staff member may leave the employ of a school, or the student may change schools, both of which would nullify the custody agreement.

Foreign nationals may enter Canada or remain in Canada without a study permit to attend a course or program of study of 6 months' duration or less [R188(1)(c)]. This exemption helps to facilitate access to short-term courses, regardless of their subject matter. The course or program of study may be part-time or full-time and should be completed within the period authorized upon entry (i.e., up to 6 months). The duration of the course or program of study is often a more important consideration than the number of months the foreign national intends to study. With the exception of exchange programs, even if foreign nationals plan to study for 6 months or less, if the course or program is longer than 6 months, they need a study permit. While a foreign national may attend a short-term course or program without a study permit at a non-DLl, they may not be issued a study permit to attend courses at a non-DLI [R216(e)].

Foreign nationals may study in Canada without a study permit to attend a course or program of study as long as it is 6 months or less in duration. The course or program of study may be part-time or full-time and should be completed within the period authorized upon entry (i.e., up to 6 months).
A professional training program is a type of additional education or training usually offered to professionals already in the field. Professional development is generally “accredited”; that is, it is recognized by an industry, association, or profession.
Professional training is offered through community colleges, universities, CEGEPs, career colleges, professional associations,
or unions.
In general, professional training programs require participants to complete both a study and work component in order to successfully complete the program, and obtain the given credential. However, unlike co-op/internship programs in post- secondary institutions (e.g., universities, community colleges) such programs often consist of a full-time work component and a part-time study component. The work component often comprises more than 50% of the study component.
Applicants wishing to participate in professional training programs must apply for a study permit to cover the study portion, if the study component is more than six months at a designated learning institution; and apply for the appropriate work permit if there is a work portion. More information can be found here: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-) citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/other- considerations.html

Hello,
I hope you and your colleagues are well. I am writing with two questions on behalf of our students at :
We have many students who transfer to our institution from other post-secondary schools in Canada and I am hoping you can clarify how the scheduled break provisions for off-campus work under R186(v) would apply to these students in their transferring terms. The Summer term (May-August) is a scheduled break for our undergraduates; however, we do have many transfer students who choose to join us in Summer as well as in Fall.
- For students who are joining our institution in Summer (starting in May), can this term still be considered a scheduled break (allowing students to work full time regardless of their course load with us) provided they were enrolled full time in an eligible program at their previous institution in the term immediately prior, and assuming they will enroll full time at our institution in the term immediately following? Note that most of these students will not have completed a credential at their previous institution but instead are transferring their credits to be used toward their degree here. They may enroll on a part-time or full-time basis for the Summer term.
- For students who have been accepted to transfer to our institution in Fall (September) and will have a break between programs before starting with us, would these students be eligible to work full time in the Summer term provided they were enrolled full time in an eligible program at their previous institution in Winter/Spring (January-April) and will enroll full time with us in September? Again, these students will not have completed a credential at their previous
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
institution so they would not fall within the provision for students who have completed a program of study as outlined in the off-campus work PDIs (as they are not holding "written confirmation of program completion from their current institution").
We have received numerous questions regarding the above from our incoming transfer students, and while it seems logical that students who meet the requirement of full-time enrollment in an eligible program in the terms immediately before and after the break should be eligible for full-time work regardless of the change in institution/program, we would not want to put our students at risk of working without authorization if this interpretation is incorrect. Therefore, any clarification you are able to provide would be much appreciated.
Thanks in advance, and please feel free to let me know if you need any additional information or clarification regarding the above in order to respond.
Warm regards,
中 Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Hello Thank you for your inquiry.
Students may work full-time off-campus during a DLl's regularly scheduled break regardless of when they transfer to the new institution. In order to work off campus without a work permit under paragraph R186(v), students must hold full-time status during the academic session before and after their regularly scheduled break.
In order for a break to be considered a regularly scheduled break, the break must be part of the DLl's academic calendar (for instance, winter and summer holidays, Reading Week). Each regularly scheduled break should not be longer than 150 days. The maximum cumulative duration of scheduled breaks is 180 days per calendar year.
Thank you,

threads.subject: Entry Into Canada For International Students -- REP-2021-0875
threads.question:
Hello,
Currently, international students may enter Canada for the purposes of pursuing primary or secondary school curriculum or a program of post-secondary study that has been confirmed by a province or territory as ready to safely host international students subject to conditions set out in the Quarantine Act, and Emergency Orders: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Mandatory Isolation) and Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order
(Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States). ).
Among other requirements to be granted entry to Canada, an international student will be required to demonstrate to a border services officer that they are entering Canada for non-discretionary purposes and that they are studying at a listed DL. If these requirements are not demonstrated by an international student upon arrival, they may be refused entry. IRCC will inform the international student through push notifications of their ability to travel based on whether a designated learning institutions has been confirmed by the province or territory as ready to host international students. International students (foreign nationals) who hold written notification from IRCC confirming the approval of their study permit application to be issued a study permit, and a letter of acceptance issued by a DLl approved by the province or territory as being ready to welcome the safe arrival of international students at the post-secondary or primary or secondary level, will be permitted to travel to Canada by air carriers (Transport Canada authority). More information can be found at this link: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/guide-international-students-arriving-abroad.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/guide-international-students-arriving-abroad.html)

threads.answer:

Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives inbox. Note that the information provided below may be of assistance but please note that we do not respond to case-specific enquiries.
For the educational requirements of Stream A of the public policy creating permanent resident pathways for Hong Kong residents, a “diploma for completion of a program that is at least 2 years in length” refers to a diploma for a post-secondary program only (not graduate or post-graduate). threads.question:

For someone who has an expiring post-graduate work permit and submitted a spousal sponsorship with a spousal open work permit last February (AOR not received yet), since they will be on maintained status, can they continue working while waiting for their SOWP or PR?
Thank you.

threads.answer:
Hello,
Question: For someone who has an expiring post-graduate work permit and submitted a spousal sponsorship with a spousal open work permit last February (AOR not received yet), since they will be on maintained status, can they continue working while waiting for their SOWP or PR?
Answer: Please note that a foreign national whose status is maintained as per paragraph 183(5) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations does not by virtue of their maintained status have authority to work. It is paragraph 186(u) of the IRPR that provides authority to work without a permit for those who are pending a decision on a work permit renewal application.
Please see the information on our public website: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: After you apply. The relevant section is copied below for ease of reference:
If you applied on paper to extend or change your work permit If you applied on paper, you won't get a letter (WP-EXT except PGWP) that proves you're authorized to work. This is because we need to make sure that your application is complete and that you meet the requirements to work.
If you applied to extend or change your work permit before it expired, you’re authorized to continue working under the same conditions as your current work permit.
You can show your employer proof that you submitted your application. Valid forms of proof include
- a copy of your work permit application
- proof that you paid your fees
- a copy of postal or courier tracking information
For more information on authority to work after applying for a work permit renewal, visit this Help Centre page.

threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
My name is registered in good standing with ICCRC.
My client has two years of Canadian work experience as a Religious Worker (NOC 4217) on an employer-specific work permit. There are employment periods when he did not receive any direct payment from the employer. According to Buddhist precepts, direct payment is not allowed. Instead, the employer had paid all necessary expenses including international and local transportation, meals, accommodation, medical expenses, and any other expenses.
My questions are as follows:
1. Will my client's Canadian work experience be qualified work experience under Express Entry-Canadian Experience Class (CEC), in terms of the fact that he has received no direct payment from the employer?
Answer: No. For the purposes of Skilled Workers under Economic Classes (Division 1 of Part 6 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations), the definition of work which applies is that defined in subsection 73(2) of the Regulations (included below).
Definition of work for the Division 1 Skilled Workers of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations
73(2) For the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned.
2. Are there any specific requirements for forms of payment regarding qualifying work experience under CEC? Will indirectly paid work experience be regarded as paid work experience under CEC?
Answer: Applicants applying through the Express Entry application management system must meet the requirements of one of the Federal Economic Classes managed through Express Entry. Work experience in all three classes must meet the definition of subsection 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), which states that work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. The deliberate phrasing of 73(2) and the use of "wages or commissions" generally excludes grants, stipends, and in-kind remuneration.
Wages and commissions are commonly understood to be monetary compensation, from an employer to an employee, for performing an activity. The onus is on the applicant to demonstrate that they were paid wages or commissions for that activity.
3. If my client is ineligible under CEC while he still wants to apply to CEC using his current work experience, will he be
eligible to apply for H&C exemption?
Answer: The foreign national cannot request Humanitarian and compassionate considerations to overcome the eligibility requirements for one of the Federal Economic Classes managed through Express Entry as a result of Section 25(1.2)(a.1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act which states the Minister may not examine the request if the request is for an exemption from any of the criteria or obligations of Division 0.1. Experience which does not meet the definition of skilled work, including the requirement that it be paid, should not be included in your client's Express Entry profile. We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

A Refugee Travel Document, which can be obtained from Passport Canada, is a document for people in Canada with
protected-person status. It is
recognized in all countries as a valid travel document; however, it cannot be used to travel to the country that the person is a citizen of or the country of claimed persecution. Further information can be found online: Refugee Travel Document requirements.
In addition, OP 16 / ENF 32 / IP 12 Passports and Travel Documents, section 7.10 Refugee Travel Document states "Refugee Travel Documents are issued by a competent authority of a country to persons recognized by that country as protected persons, pursuant to the 1951 UN Convention relating to the Status of Refugees, to facilitate the travel of the holder to other countries. The document prohibits travel to the country from which the holder fled persecution and allows the holder to return
to the issuing country within the validity period of the document”.

Applicants applying through the Express Entry application management system must meet the requirements of one of the Federal Economic Classes managed through Express Entry. Work experience in all three classes must meet the definition of subsection 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), which states that work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. The deliberate phrasing of 73(2) and the use of "wages or commissions" generally excludes grants, stipends, and in-kind remuneration.

Question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
We have a question regarding a prospective client.
Client has received the invitation under CEC class and want to retain us for PR application. Before we accept client we want make sure client is eligible for express entry and meets all requirements. I was looking but was not able to find exact information.
So I will give brief description about the scenario related to clients experience:
Scenario: Client has been working in Canada in NOC B for more than year and half. Her work hours were disruptive due to COVID. For Example: Client worked fulltime 2 weeks than part time for 1 week than off no work for one week than again fulltime for 1 week and so on. So client experience is all in a similar manner. But overall hours that client has worked are more than 1560 hours.
From (dd-mm-yyyy) To (dd-mm-yyyy)Employment Basis Hours Worked per Week
01-12-2019 25-01-2020 Full time 30 Hours 26-01-2020 26-02-2020 Part Time Average 22 hours 23-02-2020 07-03-2020 Full Time 30 Hours 08-03-2020 22-08-2020 Part TimeAverage 18 hours 23-08-2020 31-10-2020 Full Time 30 Hours 01-11-2020 09-01-2021 Part Time Average 24 hours 10-01-2021 25-05-2021 Full Time 30 Hours Total Hours = More than 1560
Please confirm if she can consider her this experience to be eligible for 1 Year CEC experience. If yes, what documents should we provide to prove her experience. Further, we have attached a template employment letter, please review if this would good enough to explain the hours details or should we provide additional details.
Answer:
It would be up to the applicant to calculate their working hours to ensure they meet the minimum work experience requirements before applying. There are a few ways to meet the 1 year of skilled work experience in Canada in the last 2
years before applying, including:
Full-time at 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours)
Equal amounts in part-time work: for example 15 hours/week for 24 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours). Applicants can work as many part-time jobs as needed to meet this requirement. Fulil-time work at more than 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months at more than 1 job (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours).
For all work experience declared, applicants must provide a reference or experience letter from the employer which indicates the number of work hours per week.
Also, please note that an allowance for a reasonable period of vacation time will generally be made in calculating the period of qualifying work experience (e.g., a two-week period of paid vacation leave within a given 52-week period in which the applicant was engaged in qualifying work experience). An allowance for normal vacation time during a period of qualifying work experience cannot be used as a substitute or proxy for meeting the in-Canada element of the work experience requirement (i.e., work experience obtained outside Canada will not be considered as though the applicant had been on a period of vacation in order to be counted as part of the period of in-Canada work experience). While officers will account for a reasonable period of vacation time in calculating the period of qualifying work experience in Canada, each application is considered on its own merits with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision.
The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements. The assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the IRCC examining officer.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,

threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Good Day,

Question: I have a question regarding Express Entry – CEC – One Year Work Experience Requirement (minimum 30 hours per week for 52 weeks per year– total 30 x 52= 1560 hours per year). When employees are paid monthly:
- How should we calculate hours per week for each month? Should we simply divide it by 4, in that case we end up calculating 48 weeks, though employee works for whole one year. Thus, how do we figure out the number of hours worked throughout 52 weeks in a year of monthly paid employment?
- We cannot add more than 30 hours to calculate 1560 hours in one year of work, so how can we calculate the total number of hours in the case of a monthly salaried employee. In addition, if an employee worked a different number of hours every month, how should the total number of hours for the complete year of employment be calculated?
Answer: It would be up to the applicant to calculate their working hours to ensure they meet the minimum work experience requirements before applying. There are a few ways to meet the 1 year of skilled work experience in Canada in the last 2 years before applying, including: Full-time at 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours) Equal amounts in part-time work: for example 15 hours/week for 24 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours). Applicants can work as many part-time jobs as needed to meet this requirement. Full-time work at more than 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months at more than 1 job (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours). For all work experience declared, applicants must provide a reference or experience letter from the employer which indicates the number of work hours per week. Please note that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

If the applicant marries and wishes the spouse to accompany after they receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA), but before they submit their application, the CRS score will change. In Express Entry, applicants are required to submit a complete electronic application for permanent residence (e-APR) within 90 calendar days of being issued an invitation to apply (ITA). Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
## Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Good day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration
Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: CRS points awarded for credentials completed 100% abroad due to Covid-19.
The applicant completed 100% ofher/his study program which started during covid from abroad. I am looking into clarifying if under EE, this applicant will still be awarded the 15-30 points on the CRS points where it refers to Canadian Credentials.
I have received different answers from the call centre which indicated that internal guide has been updated that student would be awarded regardless if they were physically in Canada or not, as long as they have been issued a Letter of Introduction
while on twitter, it has been indicated that only the ones physically in Canada would be awarded.
Answer:
For Express Entry, there have been no changes to how CRS points are awarded for education. A Canadian educational credential cannot be awarded if the credentials were obtained in a study or training program in which distance learning amounted to more than half of the program length. To get points the credential must be a “Canadian educational credential," as per R73 and meet one of the definitions of an, “Eligible credential”.
Pursuant to R73.1, a Canadian educational credential means any diploma, certificate or credential, issued on
the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is
recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such
institutions.
In addition, the credential must meet the requirements stated in the Express Entry Ministerial Instructions — MI
11(3) and MI 30 (1)-(5).
We trust that this information will assist you.

threads.subject: Unnamed LMIAs -- REP-2021-1157
threads.question:
Good day,
Can you please clarify if a name needs to be included on an LMIA prior to work permit submission? If not, and a
1*1and Cizensip Canada at Cyté Canada
ation disclosed under the Accessto Information Act Linformation divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accés à Finformation work permit is not successful for an applicant, can the same LMIA be used for another candidate, assuming that it is still valid?
Sincerely
threads.answer:
Hello,
QUESTION 1: Can you please clarify if a name needs to be included on an LMIA prior to work permit submission?
RESPONSE: Subparagraph 200(1)(c)(iii) states that a work permit may be issued if it established that "the foreign national has been offered employment, and an officer has made a positive determination under paragraphs 203(1)(a) to (e)”. This means that the positive determination must be for a specific foreign national or in plain language, the person must be named in the LMIA.
Employers can apply for an LMIA prior to having selected a worker. More information can be found on the ESDC web pages: Applying for an Unnamed Labour Market Impact Assessment However; if an employer does not provide names in their LMlA application, they must continue to try and recruit Canadians and permanent residents until they have selected a temporary foreign worker. Once they have selected a temporary foreign worker, the employer must provide the names to Service Canada for inclusion in the LMIA. After which the named foreign national may apply for a work permit. More information can be found on the ESDC web page: Hire a temporary foreign worker in a high-wage or low-wage position-After you apply
QUESTION 2: If not, and a work permit is not successful for an applicant, can the same LMIA be used for another candidate, assuming that it is still valid? RESPONSE: If the LMIA is still valid, another candidate can use it to apply for a work permit, as long as all the conditions remain the same. However, the employer must request that the names of the foreign nationals listed on the LMIA be changed to reflect the newly selected person. Please see the section: Changing names or adding information on the ESDC web page: Hire a temporary foreign worker in a high-wage or low-wage position-After you apply
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Clarification re Hong Kong PR Program-Distance Learning -- REP-2021-1045
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing to seek clarification to the new temporary public policy for PR for Hong Kong residents with regards to Education Requirements when it relates to distance learning inside Canada at a post-secondary designated learning institution (DLI) in Canada.
The Education Requirements state that: Applicants must have graduated from a DLI in the 3 years before they apply (for Stream A) OR from a DLI or with equivalent ECA in the 5 years before they apply (for Stream B) with one of the following:
a post-secondary degree (for example, bachelor's, master's, doctorate)
- a post-secondary diploma for a program of study that is at least 2 years in length a graduate or post-graduate credential for a program that is at least 1 year in length and
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
the program required them to have a post-secondary degree or diploma as a prerequisite and they graduated from their post-secondary degree or diploma no more than 5 years before the start of the graduate or post-graduate program
Furthermore for Stream A: The program of study can be completed in any field of study, with at least 50% of the program of study completed while physically present in Canada, either in class or online.
My question is, if a Hong Kong foreign national holding a valid work permit inside Canada completes a distance learning (study permit should not be required) eligible credential from a DLi while being physically present in Canada for more than 50% of the program duration within the prescribed period, would this applicant meet the Education Requirements to apply under the program?
Any guidance of the above would be greatly appreciated.
Thank you very much for your time and attention.
Respectfully,
threads.answer:
Hello,
Note that the information provided below may be of assistance but please note that we do not respond to case-specific enquiries.
To be eligible for permanent residence under stream A of the temporary public policy for Hong Kong residents, applicants must have graduated from a post-secondary designated learning institution in Canada, obtained eligible credentials as indicated on our website, and must have completed at least 50% of the program while physically present in Canada, either in person (in class) or online. Applicants may be eligible if the program of study was completed through distance learning while being physically present in Canada for at least 50% of the program of study and while being legally authorized to study in Canada.
Since by definition distance learning does not require one to be in Canada, a study permit cannot be issued for this type of course. For example, if a foreign national authorized to work in Canada is prohibited from engaging in studies as per a condition of their work permit, they are allowed to engage in distance learning courses. However, some distance learning courses include an in-Canada portion to the program (e.g., special tutorials or the writing of final exams). If the overall course of study is greater than six months, then the student requires a study permit for the in-Canada portion of the program, even if the in-Canada portion is less than six months.
We trust this information will assist you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.answer:

Answer: Candidates are assessed on whether or not they meet to requirements of the program based on the information provided in their expression of interest. In general, a student can work full-time if they're on a scheduled break, such as winter and summer holidays, or a fall or spring reading week. They're free to work overtime or work 2 part-time jobs that add up to a higher than usual number of hours. A student must be a full-time student both before and after the break to work full-time. break that comes before you start your very first school semester.
As you indicate below, some students must participate in a prerequisite English as a second language (ESL) or French as a second language (FSL) program before the start of the academic, professional or vocational program. Students in this situation are issued a study permit for the duration of the ESL or FSL program plus 1 year. threads.question:
Good morning,
Question: When initially announced the various ministers at the press conference mentioned a period of self-isolation of up to 72 hours as individuals await the results of the on-arrival test. This specific period of self-isolation is not mentioned in the relevant OlCs, can your office confirm if there is any such directive in regard to any kind of quarantine/self-isolation period while individuals await the on-arrival test?
Response: We would like to highlight that a period of isolation may vary depending on the particular circumstances of the foreign national (i.e., vaccination status and/or the time it takes to receive test results). However, as previously stated, if an isolation/quarantine period is required upon entry into Canada, the employer is required to provide the temporary foreign worker with wages substantially the same as those set out in the offer of employment.
For information on the latest requirements for vaccinated travelers, please visit: Vaccinated travellers entering Canada
If you have questions regarding the Quarantine Act, please send your inquiry to the Public Health Agency of Canada.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
threads.answer:
<RCC. - Hello,
Question: Do employers of TFWs that are engaging in the 24-72 hour self-isolation period required after their on-arrival testing have to pay them during this period (assuming they are not yet working)?
Assuming they get a negative result, does the payment obligation under IRPR 209.3 (1)(xii) apply to that brief isolation period while they await the results of their on-arrival test?
Response: As per R209.3(1)(xii), during the required quarantine period upon a foreign national's entry into Canada, the employer is required to provide the foreign national with wages substantially the same as those set out in the offer of employment. This regulation remains applicable regardless of whether the foreign national is fully vaccinated. If a foreign national is required to undergo some quarantine related isolation as per the Quarantine Act, then the employer is obligated to pay the wages under IRPR.
For more information on the new requirements please see: Government of Canada's first phase to easing border measures for travellers entering Canada
Thank you,

There is currently no single, IRCC-wide policy for the grace period for previous versions when forms are modified, though IRCC has been studying this issue. Currently, as regards the IMM 5476, IRCC advises immigration professionals of changes, as well as of the grace period for previous versions, via their professional bodies.
There is no exception to the grace period date for the IMM 5476. Even if a modification appears only “cosmetic", there would be greater confusion for users of the form, both compensated and uncompensated, and for IRCC’s various processing offices and the Client Service Centre, if an exception was made in the case of one change, but not for the other.

Requests to change DLls after applying for a study permit

threads.subject: Place of quarantine for international students -- REP-2021-1239
threads.question:
Hello,
This inquiry is about international students with a valid study permit, returning to Canada after visiting their family overseas for humanitarian reasons. As per the announced changes, if they returning to Canada after August 9, 2021, unvaccinated, they are required to have a valid PCR test before their arrival and complete a 14-days quarantine period.
Is there a mandatory requirement to complete this 14-days quarantine at a specific location arranged by a school? If there any regulation preventing a student to quarantine at their home in Canada (they have a home in Canada as they previously studied and stayed in Canada before their departure due to family emergency)?
Thank you and regards,
threads.answer:
Attachments: Quarantine and Isolation QA for International Students (July 12, 2021).pdf, Quarantine and Isolation QA for International
Students (July 12 2021)_FR....pdf,
Hello,
All international students are responsible for ensuring that they have adequate financial resources to support their quarantine and isolation plans. This is required even when seeking the fully vaccinated exemption, as final determination is made by a government representative at the border based on the information presented by international students at the time of entry into Canada. International students must be prepared to quarantine for 14 days in the event that they are symptomatic and/or do not meet the requirements for the fully vaccinated exemptions. Upon arrival, international students must be able to demonstrate that they have a plan in place and the means to support their initial 14-day mandatory quarantine and isolation period in Canada. Failure to do so may result in fines of up to $5,000Cdn under the Contraventions Act. International students must ensure that they have prepared themselves according to accurate information attained from reliable sources regarding their responsibilities set out in the Emergency Order under the Quarantine Act such as Government of Canada social media, or social media communications provided by their designated learning institution.
For more information, please see consult the attached Q&A document.
Thank you kindly,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Points for Arranged Employment (FSW and CEC) -- (REP-2021-0775) -- REP-2021-0991
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience.
Question: Does an applicant for PR under CEC or FSW who receives points for arranged employment based on the fact that they have obtained an LMiA and employer specific Work Permit have to maintain a valid employer specific Work Permit throughout the processing of their PR application to maintain their arranged employment points? OR, can the applicant, once eligible to do so, apply for a bridging Work Permit to continue working for the same employer and still maintain their arranged employment points?
Answer: No, the applicant is not required to maintain the same valid employer-specific work permit while we process their application, but must continue to meet the criteria for arranged employment points as per section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions in order to keep their CRS points. This means that if the applicant is eligible for, and obtains a BOWP, they would keep their CRS points as long as their new work permit meets the criteria listed under section 29(2). Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements, and any change in circumstance should be communicated to IRCC.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox
threads.answer:

The applicant may be eligible for a bridging open work permit (BOWP) which lets the applicant continue working while waiting for the results of their permanent residence application. Eligibility and applications can be found on our website.

threads.subject: Does SDS stream require additional financial documents ? -- REP-2021-1250
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
We would like to confirm if additional proof of funds documents are required for the new SDS stream, such as Bank statements, Tax files, pay stubs, employment letter or business ownership certificate OR if only proof of GIC
investment is enough to suffice application requirements under this stream.
The requirement to be accepted as an SDS applicant is proof of a $10,000 GIC held by an eligible financial institution, so the GIC on its own is sufficient for application. That said, it is always a good idea to show additional funds available to the applicant, especially because $10,000 is seen as the basic amount required to support a student once tuition and travel are paid, with no room to deal with emergencies or additional unforeseen costs.
Also, we would like to confirm if the amount of CAD$ 10,000 for the GIC is the requirement for all applicants regardless of the accompanying family members in the application.
The other applicants must show sufficient funds to meet their costs.
The following base amounts will help to assess financial sufficiency. The base amount for students includes all
requirements related to transportation and maintenance, including the cost of books, equipment, and supplies. The
size of the community where the student is destined is not a consideration.
- Student base: $10,000 for twelve-month period, prorated at $833 per month, plus cost of tuition.
- Spouse/common-law partner/first family member base-$4,000 for twelve-month period prorated at $333 per month – Dependent child/subsequent family member base-$3,000 for twelve-month period per dependent child of any age, prorated at $255 per month.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Inquiry on eTA and Restoration of Study Permit -- REP-2021-1148
threads.question:
Good day,
Restoration of status cannot be granted at the port of entry. If a foreign national leaves Canada, they will be deemed to be seeking a new entry on their return, and the previous non-compliance with imposed conditions may make them inadmissible to Canada as per section A41 and subsection A29(2). Foreign nationals who have failed to comply with the conditions imposed under section R185 need to apply in Canada for restoration of their status or leave Canada immediately. During the processing of a restoration application, should an officer determine that the foreign national has left Canada, the officer shall refuse the application as the foreign national is no longer eligible to apply for restoration. More information can be found here: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/temporary-residents/visitors/restoration-status.html We trust that this information will assist you.

threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience.
Question: We understand that IRCC has a new temporary policy in place with regard to medical exams for inland PR applicants ([https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/temporary-public-policy-exempting-some-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/temporary-public-policy-exempting-some-) foreign-nationals-canada-requiring-immigration-medical-exam.html).
Based on the information available on IRCC's website we note that applicants must meet all of the criteria noted below. However, the last bullet point is ambiguous, in that applicants and immigration representatives do not have a reliable method of confirming exactly what an IRCC medical officer noted with regard to a previous medical exam that may have been conducted up to 5 years ago. In most cases these days, our firm is only able to obtain the IME sheet like the attached sample from our clients. However, ther IME sheet only confirms when the medical exam was conducted, and does not give any indication of how an IRCC medical officer may evaluate the results. Applicants may have forgotten what occurred 5 years ago and we do not have access to this information. Given that it is not uncommon for EE cases to get refused as incomplete for very trivial reasons as opposed to the officer sending a request for more information, we are finding that applicants are extremely wary of this new exemption and would rather just complete a new medical exam to avoid any potential reasons for an unfair refusal of their Express Entry case.
Could you please clarify whether IRCC intends to provide more information as to how the exemption will be applied? Are we to assume that by virtue of a previous temporary residence application getting approved in the past, the IRCC medical officer must have found no issues with the old medical? If so, will IRCC be posting an update on the website to make this more clear to the public?
Answer: If an applicant meets the criteria as listed in the temporary public policy, we ask that they submit a copy of their previous immigration medical exam, or unique medical identifier number from their previous examination (whichever the panel physician provided them upon completion of their original exam). If an applicant was previously deemed a high risk to public health and safety, they would have been notified by IRCC of their results, or could have potentially been deemed inadmissible to Canada. We would recommend that if applicants believe they qualify under the temporary public policy, they should submit their previous medical identifiers, and if for some reason we are unable to use their previous examination, we will contact those individuals to undergo a new medical examination or discuss next steps. This information is included in the public policy. Please note that the instructions for Medical exams for Express Entry have also been updated, indicating what applicants should submit depending on their physical location, and if they've previously had a medical exam.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Clarification sought re new Fully Vaccinated quarantine exemption and R209.2 -- REP-2021-1328
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives
mailbox.
Question: Is there a requirement on the employer's part to start paying the foreign national under R209.2 during the first two weeks they are in Canada, where they do not have to quarantine. So Foreign Nationals who are exempt from quarantine do not have to be paid until their official start date in Canada? Or, does 209.2(1)(a)(iii) supersede (vii)? E.g. that no matter when the foreign national arrives in Canada and is issued the work permit, the employer must start paying on the day of arrival even if the foreign national entered Canada in advance of the offer of employment's official start date?
Response: As per 209.2(1)(a)(vii), the employer must pay for the quarantine period upon entry regardless of the day on which the work begins. For example, if the worker is vaccinated but upon entry is discovered that they have COVID-19 and an isolation/quarantine period is mandated under the Quarantine Act, the employeris required to provide the temporary foreign worker with wages substantially the same as those set out in the offer of employment.
Please be advised that we cannot provide case-specific advice as CBSA officers at the Port of Entry make a decision based on the particular circumstances and the supporting documentation. If a foreign national seeks admission to Canada well in advance of the start date stated in Offer of Employment, CBSA officers may ask questions related as to the reasons for early admission. We would like to highlight that the onus is always on the foreign national seeking entry to Canada, to satisfy the Port of Entry officer that they are admissible to Canada and that they meet the requirements in order to be issued a work permit.
Forinformation on the latest requirements for vaccinated travelers, please visit: Vaccinated travellers entering Canada
If you have questions regarding the Quarantine Act, please send your inquiry to the Public Health Agency of Canada.

threads.answer:
Ministerial Instructions EE A15(3), (4) and 25(2) and Regulated Professions -- REP-2021-1295
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: When evaluating whether an applicant has performed the lead statement and duties of a NOC Unit Group, does IRCC consider the applicant's license or certification status in a regulated profession in cases of mandatory regulation in the jurisdiction/province/territory where the work experience was obtained? In other words, can an applicant be considered to have performed the duties and lead statement of a NOC Unit Group even if they are not regulated/certified/licensed in an occupation with a mandatory certification/licensing/regulation requirement stated in that NOC Unit Group?
Answer: Yes, when an Immigration Officer reviews an application, they will review the license or certification status of the applicant compared to the provincial or territorial requirements. Officers must be satisfied that applicants have not only performed the actions described in the lead statement of the occupational description of the NOC, but also performed a substantial number of the main duties, including all the essential duties. If an applicant does not have the mandatory employment requirements (schooling, certification, licensing), then the Officer would not be satisfied that they'd be able to perform the duties of the job. NOC positions list whether or not a certification or license is mandatory. An example would be NOC 7237– Welders and related machine operators, which lists the schooling requirements, and in which provinces or
territories the certification is compulsory or voluntary.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox
