Question: I have a question regarding Continuous work experience for FSW. If someone is working part-time continuously for a university but its contract based and the University closes for Christmas break leaving 7 days between the old contract ending and the new contract beginning does this make them ineligible for Federal Skilled Worker for work experience? They have some breaks that are between 2-7 days between contracts due to the University schedules. I think this may be considered non-continuous work experience?
Answer: Yes, a break between contracts would constitute a gap in employment, and would not be considered continuous work. The applicant must show that for a continuous year (which can be met in various ways, as indicated on our website) they performed the duties set out in the lead statement of the occupational description of the NOC.
Question: Also can someone work 8 months full-time then finish the rest of the hours part-time for the 24 months if it's the same NOC code and employer? A combination of full time and part time to make up the 1 year of continuous work experience.
Answer: Yes, as is stated on our website, an applicant can meet the requirement for 1 year of continuous work in a few different ways, as long as the applicant meets the 1,560 hours total, and does not work more than 30 hours per week. For part-time work, applicants can also work more than 15 hours a week as long as it contributes to 1,560 total hours. Please ensure the applicant provides supporting documentation which shows how they gained the work experience.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,

RE: CLARIFICATION: Caregiver PILOT-Canadian Education Requirements from PRIVATE
Dear
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representative Mailbox. Note that we cannot respond to case-specific questions, but have provided some information based on the general scenarios that you have outlined below. Also note that updates to Program Delivery Instructions (PDI) were already underway, and the update will include information on Canadian education credentials.
1. If the FN has 1-year of post-secondary education from a PRIVATE institution and not a degree or diploma, is THIS diploma or certificate ACCEPTABLE for HCCP (CAREGIVER) or HSWP program? A post-secondary Canadian educational credential is any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential that is issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions. As such, an applicant who has started a college or university program and has successfully completed the credits for one year of that program, but who has not yet completed the program of study, would not meet this requirement.
2. If the FN finishes ONLINE in Canada (distance learning) the 1-year post-secondary diploma or certificate from a PRIVATE institution and not the DEGREE program, is this DIPLOMA acceptable for HCCP and HSWP program? The requirement for Canadian education under the HCCP or HSW classes is to have any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential that is issued on the completion of a one-year Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions. Please clarify and provide the Policy or Bulletin or Regulations. Section 1 of the Ministerial instructions for the Home Child Care Provider and Home Support Worker Classes indicates that "Canadian educational credential has the same meaning as in subsection 73(1) of the Regulations", which means any secondary school diploma* or any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential that is issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions. *Note that the education requirements under HCCP/HSW specify to have a one-year post-secondary (or higher) educational credential. Therefore, “any secondary school diploma" would not apply.
We trust this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

RE: Use of Auth. Rep. Portal VS Newly launched portals-Enquiry from RCIC
Good day,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox.
Please see the responses to your questions below:
Do we continue to use our Authorized Rep Portal for TR and PR applications or should start using the new portals launched by IRCC from now on?
At this time, licensed representatives should continue to use the Authorized Paid Representative (APR) Portal to submit the following types of applications on behalf of their clients:
Visitor visa, study and work permit applications Express Entry applications International Experience Canada (IEC) applications Electronic travel authorization (eTA) applications Interim Federal Health Program (IFHP) applications
For more details about using the APR portal please visit: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/partners-service-providers/authorized-paid-representatives-portal.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/partners-service-providers/authorized-paid-representatives-portal.html)
Other categories of PR applications (non-express entry) can now be submitted by representatives on behalf of their clients using the PR Representative Portal: [https://prson-srpel.apps.cic.gc.ca/en/rep/login](https://prson-srpel.apps.cic.gc.ca/en/rep/login)
Once a PR application submitted through the PR Representative Portal receives an acknowledgement of receipt letter, it can then be linked to your APR portal account.
Would there be any difference in processing time or priority/expedite processing if we use the new portals compared to the Authorized Rep Portal?
Applications being submitted through client facing portals (such as the Permanent Residence Portal, the IRCC Secure account or the IRCC portal) are not prioritized over applications submitted through the APR portal or the Representative PR portal. While certain applications may be prioritized based on departmental/ministerial priorities, they are not prioritized or expedited based on the portal through which they are received.
Are there any categories of applications which are now completely done online, and the paper applications are discontinued?
Please consult the instruction guides on the IRCC website for each program to determine how the applications can or should be submitted as it varies from program-to-program and this information is updated on an ongoing basis.
There are a number of application categories where both paper and online applications are still currently being accepted. Meanwhile, there are also other programs where applicants have to apply online (such as Parents and Grandparents, or in-Canada TRs seeking to extend their temporary resident status/authorization to study or work); however paper applications may still be available under certain circumstances such as for those who require accommodation as a result of a disability; if there's a problem with the online application (i.e. system restrictions); or other exceptional circumstances beyond the applicant's control. Please consult the instructions for each program for more details.
If you require further clarification regarding whether paper applications are still being accepted for a specific program or if you have questions regarding requesting alternate formats, please contact IRCC.
Is it ok to still use paper application despite the submission is possible using the newly launched portals?
It is still acceptable to use paper applications where it is specified in the program instructions as an option. As noted above, some programs will only accept paper applications in exceptional circumstances and this will be specified in the program instructions.
We trust this information will assist you.

threads.question: I would like to have functional guidance on the application assessment process for Express Entry applicants who have been issued COPR but have not landed yet to obtain their PR status and get married after being issued COPR. When such applicants notify IRCC to include their dependent spouses after getting COPR and before landing, is the assessment always carried out again to ensure that the all the eligibility requirements, inadmissibility requirements and CRS threshold requirements applicable at the time of ITA are still being met?
threads.answer:
Section A11.2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act does not apply when an applicant adds a family member to their application after their application for permanent residence has been submitted, however all family members must be examined, whether they are accompanying the principal applicant or not. Family members can be added to the application at any time during the process, prior to obtaining permanent resident status. If the applicant's marital status or family composition changes (e.g. marriage, common-law relationship, separation, divorce, birth of a child, adoption of a child, death, etc) after they have submitted an application for permanent residence, they must notify IRCC immediately either by writing to the IRCC office email address mentioned on their approval letter or through the IRCC webform. An officer will re-open the application to assess the recently added family member. Please note any family member who has not been examined prior to the applicant becoming a permanent resident will not be permitted to be sponsored by the applicant in the future.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Enquiry in Regard to Chinese Birth Certificate -- REP-2021-1862
threads.question: Does IRCC accept a Notarized Kinship certificate with birth date details (Chinese and English) as an alternative to a Birth Certificate, along with a valid Chinese Passport? If not, what identification/ documentation would be acceptable to IRCC?
threads.answer:
If the applicant is from China (and not Mongolia) - IRCC request the applicant to submit a copy of their original hospital birth certificate. For children born in the People's Republic of China, IRCC ask the applicants to submit a scanned notarized copy of the original Medical Certificate of Birth issued by the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China. When this document is not available, applicants must submit an explanation as to why this document cannot be submitted. However, the Medical Certificate of Birth issued by the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China started to be available only after 1996. Applicants who were born before that date would not have access to this document. IRCC have noted that the birth certificate for Mongolian is somehow a little different from the rest of China as it is present in a booklet format (not a one-page certificate). In order to confirm the applicant's identity, applicant submit a Notarized Kinship certificate that includes birth date details along with a valid Passport, National Identity Card, and an explanation as to why they are unable to submit the birth certificate.
If applicant coming from Inner Mongolia (province of China) - IRCC does not accept Notarized Kinship certificate as a substitute for Birth Certificate for Chinese citizens. Instead, we would request Hospital birth records and a copy of a Hukou (Family Registration booklet) as a start. Local school registration documents also show names of parents and can be used as an alternative proof. For Chinese nationals who were born before January 1, 1996, there is no standard official birth certificate, and in some rural area, birth records can be difficult to obtain. An applicant can obtain a Notarized Kinship certificate or Notarized birth certificate by submitting their birth record (or if not available, a certificate issued by local government or community office), their ID card, Hukou to a local notary office. A Notarized Kinship certificate or Notarized birth certificate, combined with other civil documents and evidence, can be treated as alternative proof. If the applicant is unable to prove the family link for their dependent(s), the visa office may require a DNA test as a last option.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The reviewing officer could always request more documents if there are concerns with the applicants' submission. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
Sincerely,

Nous comptons parmi nos élèves, dix-sept étudiants étrangers qui ont reçu une lettre d'approbation de permis d'études, mais qui n'ont jamais reçu le permis en tant que tel, même après que 6 semaines se soient écoulées depuis l'émission de la lettre d'approbation.
Il est indiqué sur les lettres d'approbation de permis d'études qu'elles ne constituent pas des titres de séjour pour demeurer au Canada.
En tant qu'institution, pouvons-nous considérer qu'une lettre d'approbation de permis d'études est suffisante pour permettre l'inscription d'un étudiant étranger?
Dans l'attente de votre retour, veuillez recevoir nos salutations distinguées.
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Bonjour,
Pour les étudiants à l’intérieur du Canada, une lettre d’approbation n’est pas suffisante pour permettre l’inscription d’un étudiant étranger, à moins qu’une autorisation d’étudier y soit clairement indiquée. Les informations indiquées sur la lettre d’approbation prennent autorité.
Aussi prendre en compte que le paragraphe 189 indique que l’étranger qui fait une demande en vertu du paragraphe 217(1) est autorisé à étudier au Canada sans permis d’études jusqu’à la décision sur sa demande s’il est demeuré au Canada depuis l’expiration de son permis d’études et qu’il continue à se conformer aux conditions dont est assorti le
permis, exception faite de la date d’expiration.
Pour plus d’informations, veuillez également vous référer à notre site internet.
Nous espérons que ces informations vous seront utiles.

threads.answer:
### Bonjour, Question :
La « vérification de l’exhaustivité » d’une DRP est-elle confirmée par l’émission d’un accusé de réception avec # temporaire ou un accusé de réception avec # définitif est-il requis ?
Réponse :
C’est l’accusé de réception avec un numéro définitif qui est requis.
IRCC s'est engagé à émettre des accusés de réception (ADR) modifiés pour informer les clients que leurs dossiers a été reçu et est en attente de traitement. Ces ADR ont un numéro temporaire.

Is this correct? If yes, the understanding is such a student would NOT need to apply for a restoration of immigration status but can simply go ahead with their PGWP application (as long as student applies in 180 days from getting transcript or program completion letter and meets other eligibility requirements). threads.answer:
Good day,
Below are clarifications to your inquires:
- For those who apply for a study permit with a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) which states 'Yes' in the 'Internship/work practicum' section of LOA, does the applicant need to also include a completed IMM 5710 form (for requesting processing of a co-op/internship work permit) along with their study permit application? If not, is the co-op/internship/work practicum work permit automatically processed with their study permit application? If the client selected 'yes' when applying for a study permit then IRCC will process a co-op work permit automatically. Students are only required to fill out the study permit application and IRCC will process a co-op work permit with their study permit application at the same time. When an applicant submits a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) which states 'Yes' in the 'Internship/work practicum' section of LOA with their study permit application and their application is eventually approved but, for some unknown reason, applicant is not issued a co-op/internship/work practicum work permit, can the applicant request re-consideration of their application so that likely a co-op/internship/work practicum work permit may be issued? If not, are there any other options to pursue? Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case-specific advice. For case-specific enquiries, please contact the Client Support Centre. [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/client-support-centre.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/client-support-centre.html) If the LOA of certain study programs such as an Early Childhood Education Diploma states, under 'Conditions of acceptance' section, "For work practicum purposes students must complete a standard First Aid with CPR Level C within the 1st month of program start", would such a condition hinder the issuance of a co-op/internship/work practicum work permit in any way? The eligibility requirements for a co-op permit is to have a valid study permit; work is required to complete the study program in Canada; a letter from the school that confirms all students in the program need to complete work placements to get their degree, and the co-op placement or internship totals 50% or less of the study program. For more information on co-op permits please visit our website. In the Winter 2022 term, can a student start their study program, online, while residing outside Canada, as long as they apply for a study permit before starting their study program (and their study permit must eventually be approved), while counting the time spent studying online towards the length of a post-graduate work permit? All students that were enrolled in a PGWP-eligible program in progress in March 2020 or started a program of study from spring 2020 up to and including the fall 2021 semester are not required to complete 50% of their program (or programs) of study in Canada. Up to 100% of their program can be completed online from outside
Canada. Time spent studying outside of Canada can be counted towards the overall length of the post-graduation work permit until December 31, 2021. For more information please visit our website.
However, any time spent studying outside of Canada after December 31, 2021 should be deducted from the length of the post-graduation work permit and will not be counted towards the length of a PGWP.
In the Winter 2022 (W22) term, can a study permit holder residing inside Canada study online while maintaining eligibility towards a PGWP IF some of the W22 in-person classes have been moved to an online-only format because of COVID-19?
If students are inside of Canada and their in-person classes in Canada have been moved to an online-only format and they are taking their classes online because of COVID-19, then they may be eligible PGWP. If a designated learning institution offers a hybrid or “hyflex” model it is recommended that the student attend in- class portions when possible. For more information please refer to our website. Please note this guidance refers to Fall 2021 and is not applicable to Winter 2022.
When a student completes a study program and lets their study permit expire (e.g., 90 days from program completion) but has a co-op work permit with expiry date several months out in the future, considering section 209 of IRPR (Regulations), it appears student has a valid immigration status in Canada until the expiry date of co-op work permit even though their immigration status as a student already expired. Is this correct? If yes, the understanding is such a student would NOT need to apply for a restoration of immigration status but can simply go ahead with their PGWP application (as long as student applies in 180 days from getting transcript or program completion letter and meets other eligibility requirements). Is this understanding accurate?
A co-op work permit does not confer a foreign national's temporary resident status and that the co-op work permit must be issued with a valid study permit. Students who have completed their program of study are allowed to work under paragraph 186(w) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations [while they are waiting for a decision on their post-graduation work permit application if they meet the eligibility requirements as per our website.
Please note applications are assessed on an individual basis, and officers must be satisfied that all requirements are met. In order to render a decision as mandated by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations, officers consider various factors. These factors help demonstrate that the applicant's intent to become a temporary resident is bona fide. Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
I hope that this information is helpful to you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.answer:
November 16, 2021 4:21 PM
FW: Q about Residency obligation of PR -- REP-2021-1496
1. If the client waits until the expiry of their PR card to return to Canada, they will be required to apply for a permanent resident travel document (PRTD) for which a residency obligation will be assessed. There are no exceptions for meeting residency obligations during the pandemic, however, the client can describe their situation by applying for humanitarian and compassionate consideration on their PRTD application.
2. The examination of residency status begins on the day that the application is received. It is sufficient for those who have been permanent residents for 5 years or more to demonstrate that they have met their residency requirements in the 5 years immediately before examination, or if they have been permanent residents for less than 5 years to demonstrate that they will be able to meet their residency requirement using the day they became a permanent resident as the starting date (PR since date).
3. Designated officers with the authority to assess humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) considerations will consider all the information they have, including a client's submission of their personal circumstances that they feel would justify retention of their permanent resident status, despite not having met their residency obligation. The designated officer with the authority to assess H&C would take into account the best interests of a child directly affected by the determination, and the degree of hardship that may be caused by a determination that an individual or family has lost permanent resident status. Also, a permanent resident complies with the residency obligation if the permanent resident they are accompanying is their spouse or common-law partner or parent and that spouse or common-law partner or parent is in compliance with their residency obligation, as per A28(2)(a)(iv).

IRCC will only make corrections or changes to a eCoPR/CoPR if there was a mistake made by IRCC. threads.answer:
Expires: February 15, 2022 12:00 AM
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question:
I have an applicant who is employed full-time in Canada and holds a work permit and a TRP. She has held this TRP for at least 3 years continuously. The applicant is now looking to apply for permanent residence. I have the following questions:
1. When an applicant is extending the TRP inland, does being on implied status constitute a break in continuity?;
2. Does the applicant's daughter have to submit a separate application for PR?; and
3. What is the process? Does the applicant submit an EE profile and then submit additional docs with respect to the TRP Holder category? Or is it a paper based application?
Answer:
1. A subsequent TRP may be issued after the expiry of the previous TRP without a break in continuity if
- the client applied before the expiry of the TRP (following similar principles of maintained status [previously implied status] in that the client shouldn't suffer a break in status due to processing times) the applicant's circumstances warrant a subsequent TRP
Please note, employed full-time temporary resident permit (TRP) holders who are in Canada may extend their temporary resident status by applying for a subsequent TRP, using application form Application to Change Conditions, Extend My Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker form [IMM 5710]. There are no extensions of existing TRPs.
2. The applicant's daughter will be included on her mother's PR application if she is a dependant.
3. It depends on the line of business, which the applicant is applying to as to the process. As the applicant has a TRP they would be best to apply for permanent residence under the permit holder class. This class doesn't fall under EE. The client is welcome to pick whatever line of business they would like which they qualify for. For more information: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/permanent-residence/non-economic-classes/permits.html We trust that this information will assist you. Sincerely,
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Renewal of visa on renewal of passport -- REP-2021-1394
threads.question:
Dear ImmRep,
Could you please provide clarity on the question below?:
Question: Upon renewal of passports, are foreign nationals with Canadian visa counterfoils in their passports required to re-apply for the visa counterfoils on the expired passport, or does the visa automatically get carried forward to the renewed passport?
For Example- X’s passport is expiring in 3 years. X applies for a Super Visa (10- years). X receives a 10-year Super Visa. In 2023, X applies for a renewal of their passport. X receives their new passport with all blank pages. Does the 10-year Super Visa now stand canceled, or does its validity automatically get carried over to the new passport?
Any thoughts would be appreciated. Thank you for your time and attention to this query.
Regards,
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
Temporary resident visas (including super visas) are issued to the validity of the passport, less one month —up to a maximum duration of 10 years. So, when the foreign national's passport expires, they will have to apply for a new visa.

Bonjour,
Oui, IRCC traite et finalise actuellement des demandes et ce partout dans le monde.
Les migrations mondiales sont perturbées par la pandémie. Des restrictions de voyage généralisées aux contraintes imposées à nos partenaires d’établissement, en passant par le télétravail des employés, les répercussions sur le système d'immigration du Canada ont été considérables.
Le ministère avait aussi accordé la priorité au traitement des demandes des candidats qui étaient déjà au Canada, mais aujourd'hui, le traitement des demandes à l’étranger est en vigueur.
IRCC a toutefois agi rapidement et fait beaucoup de chemin depuis le début de la pandémie en offrant des ressources additionnelles là ou les besoins sont les plus grands, simplifiant nos processus et augmentant la capacité des systèmes. Nous avons également entrepris une modernisation sans précédent du système d'immigration, grâce à plus de 800 millions de dollars du budget 2021 pour créer une toute nouvelle plateforme numérique pour gérer les cas d'immigration. Cette nouvelle plateforme transformera notre système d'immigration, ce qui signifie que les dossiers seront traités plus rapidement et que les travailleurs arriveront plus tôt.
Nous savons que ces perturbations ont eu un impact sérieux sur de nombreuses personnes qui espéraient commencer une nouvelle vie au Canada, et nous les remercions pour leur patience dans ces moments difficiles.
IRCC est responsable des évaluations relatives à l’admissibilité, y compris de l’évaluation médicale et de l’évaluation de sécurité. IRCC accordera la résidence permanente au demandeur une fois que toutes les exigences relatives à l’admissibilité seront satisfaites.
Merci
La boîte aux lettres des représentants de l'immigration

threads.answer:
immigration Kepresentatives / Représentants immigration (IRCC)
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: In an Express Entry profile and e-APR, specifically the "Work History" section, are candidates required to fill in all of their work experience in the past 10 years? Or can they declare only the work experience they wish to claim CRS points for, and fill in the rest in the personal history section in their e-APR? I note that when candidates declare work experience they don't receive points for in the Work History section, upload fields are generated automatically even if they don't receive CRS points or don't wish to claim CRS points for.
Similarly for the "Education History" section, are candidates required to fill in all of their secondary and post-secondary education? Or can they declare only the highest education which they get CRS points for, and fill in the rest in the personal history section in their e-APR?

threads.subject: Spouse's Siblings points, if spouse dies or is non-accompanying in Express Entry -- REP-2021-1930
threads.question: If PA's spouse dies or is not accompanying, will the PA still get 5 points in FSW and 15 points in CRS for the (dead or non-accompanying) spouse's PR/Canadian sibling in Canada?
threads.answer:
The applicant would earn 15 points in CRS, if the applicant's spouse is not accompanying. The applicant would not earn 5 points in FSW, if the applicants' spouse is dead.
MI — Points for sibling in Canada: 31 (1) Fifteen points may be assigned to a foreign national if either they or their accompanying spouse or common-law partner has at least one sibling who is:
(a) 18 years or older;
- (b) a Canadian citizen or permanent resident; and
(c) living in Canada.
IRPR 83(5) Family relationships in Canada
(5) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), a skilled worker shall be awarded 5 points if:
(a) the skilled worker or the skilled worker's accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner is
related by blood, marriage, common-law partnership or adoption to a person who is 18 years or older, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada and who is
(i) their father or mother, (ii) the father or mother of their father or mother, (iii) their child, (iv) a child of their child,
(v) a child of their father or mother, (vi) a child of the father or mother of their father or mother, other than their father or mother, or (vii) a child of the child of their father or mother.
Please note that while changing partner's status from “non-accompanying" to “accompanying” during the processing of an application, up to the time of landing, may not constitute misrepresentation; however, this choice was never intended to be used as a strategy. Rather, it allows families to describe accurately their situations and intentions and to comply with section 16 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act on the obligation to answer truthfully. The principal applicant's Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score will be recalculated to account for the change in situation, at all points in the process.
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The reviewing officer could always request more documents if there are concerns with the applicants' submission. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentations to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

threads.answer:

Good day,
Since September 7th, 2021, the Government of Canada has allowed fully vaccinated foreign nationals to enter Canada for discretionary (non-essential) travel. This exemption from travel restrictions does not require written authorization from IRCC, however foreign nationals are still subject to other requirements, such as pre-entry molecular testing, random on-arrival testing and uploading the requested information in ArriveCAN.

Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox.

If you are still unable to create your existing Authorized Paid Representative Portal account, you must create a new GCKey and submit a new enrolment request. You must indicate on the enrolment form that you have a previous Portal account by answering "NO” to the question that asks about a successful previous enrolment. This allows our technical team to merge the new account with the existing one. This process does not impact any of your existing applications.
Please follow the steps below to re-enrol:
1. Create a new GCKey.
2. Submit a new portal enrolment request (find out how using our enrolment guide).
3. When you complete the enrolment form, indicate that you were not previously enrolled.
We trust this will assist you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.answer:
IRCC uses the National Occupation Classification (NOC) and the Labour Market Impact Assessment to determine the employment requirements for specific occupations. In some occupations it depends on the province of destinations whether certification is required or not. Using your example of NOC 7313 - Heating, refrigeration and air conditioning mechanics the certification would not be required if the applicant was destined to British Columbia but would be if destined to Alberta.
Employment requirements
- Completion of secondary school and training courses or a vocational program is usually required.
- Completion of a three- to five-year apprenticeship program or a combination of over five years of work experience and industry courses in refrigeration and air conditioning repair is usually required to be eligible for trade certification.
- Trade certification for refrigeration and air conditioning mechanics is compulsory in Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Quebec, Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta and available, but voluntary, in all other provinces and the territories.
- Trade certification for transport refrigeration mechanics is available, but voluntary, in New Brunswick and Alberta.
- Red Seal endorsement is also available to qualified refrigeration and air conditioning mechanics upon successful completion of the interprovincial Red Seal examination.

Question:
My question is regarding eligibility requirements for Bridging open work permit for permanent residence applicants.
There used to be a requirement that one cannot apply for this type of work permit more than 4 months before the current work permit expiry date. Current instructions on the website do not mention this requirement.
The Question is: Can a permanent resident applicant who has an employer-restricted work permit that expires in more than 4 months (let's say in 8 months) apply for a bridging open work permit, provided other requirements are met (no employment restrictions, PR application AOR etc.)?
Answer: The 4-month requirement was removed from the Bridging open work permit (BOWP) program delivery instructions on September 16, 2021. Among other eligibility criteria, the applicant must meet one of the following requirements:
0 have valid temporary resident status and authorization to work as the holder of a valid work permit 0 have maintained status and authorization to work under paragraph 186(u) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) as a result of submitting an application to renew their work permit under subsection R201(1) obe eligible to restore their temporary resident status with authorization to work on a work permit
We suggest that foreign workers check processing times for work permit from inside Canada prior to submitting their BOWP application to ensure their application will be finalized before the expiry of their current work permit.

threads.subject: TRV for Supervisa Parents Visa Required Countries -- REP-2021-1259 -- REP-2021-1432
threads.question:
Further to my question below, could you please clarify how applicants can obtain a RE-ENTRY visa in their passports if they want to travel to the US for e.g. WITHOUT being able to apply for a Supervisa from outside Canada if they are residents inside Canada?
Kind regards,
and Cizenship Caneda
threads.answer:
November 24, 2021 9:02 AM
RE: TRV for Supervisa Parents Visa Required Countries -- REP-2021-1259 --
Good day,
Thank you for your enquiry.
It appears that you are confusing several concepts: temporary resident visa (TRV), temporary status and visitor record
(VR).
A TRV (including a super visa) is a multiple entry visa that is valid for up to 10 years. A TRV is the counterfoil that is placed in a passport that allows a foreign national to travel to Canada. It authorizes multiple entries to Canada for the duration of the visa; however, it does not give the foreign national temporary status in Canada.
It is only upon entry to Canada that a foreign national obtains temporary status. Foreign nationals can apply to extend their status. If approved, a VR would be issued as proof of their temporary status in Canada.
If a foreign national's TRV (including super visas) expires while they are in Canada, this does not affect their temporary
resident status. They can remain in Canada until the end of their authorized temporary stay.
A TRV on the other hand (whether or not a super visa) cannot be extended or issued automatically along with a VR. Once a TRV expires, an application for a new visa must be submitted if the applicant wishes to leave Canada and return. Only foreign nationals with a valid work or study permit may apply for a TRV from within Canada. If the foreign national wants to apply for a super visa, the application must be submitted and obtained outside Canada. A stay of up to two years for super visa holders is given at the port of entry by a Border Services Officer.
As mentioned above, if they wish to extend their stay, they may apply to do so by submitting an Application to Change
Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Visitor: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-)
citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html.
A person's temporary resident status ends on the earliest of The day on which the foreign national leaves Canada; The day on which their Visitor Record or permit becomes invalid; or The day on which the initial period of authorized stay ends.
I hope this provides clarity.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
Thank you for your reply. However, the question was this:
The applicant has a work permit pursuant an LMIA application in NOC 0711 The job offer from the employer is in NOC 0016 – same employer as indicated on the work permit
Nothing in the regulations states that the job offer must be in an occupation similar to that on the work permit or the LMIA, only that it has bto be issued by the same employer as on the work permit
Will a candidate be awarded the 200 points if their work permit they have is in NOC A, the LMIA was for NOC A, they have been working for 12+ months in NOC the A job, but the offer is for NOC 0016?
Thank you,
threads.answer:
Expires:February 20, 2022 12:00 AM
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: Will a candidate be awarded the 200 points if their work permit they have is in NOC A, the LMIA was for NOC A, they have been working for 12+ months in NOC the A job, but the offer is for NOC 0016?
Answer: Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case-specific advice.
We would like to highlight that arranged employment is defined in subsection 82(2) of the Regulations. Points for arranged employment must meet the requirements of section 29 of the Express Entry Ministerial Instructions (MIs). The offer must meet one of the requirements outlined in section 29(2) of the MIs.
Applicants may claim 200 points for arranged employment with a valid NOC 00 job offer without having a work permit for a NOC 00 occupation. However, please note that subsection 29(3) of the MIs also applies, therefore, the applicant has to provide evidence that they are able and likely to agree to perform the duties of the offer of employment for the points to be granted. As you are aware, the onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,

Hello,
When establishing a client's name, IRCC relies upon the Machine readable zone (MRZ) of the passport. Passports that are compliant with the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards, will not allow for special characters in the MRZ. Therefore, the recording of the applicant's name without the special character should not impede travel.
IRCC systems can only record characters found in the Roman alphabet and the following French accents: â, à, é, ê, ë, è, i, î, ô, ü, ù, û, ç. IRCC documents can only be printed with characters found in the Roman alphabet and the French accents previously mentioned.
For more information, please refer to our Naming procedures: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-) citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/identity-management/naming-procedures.html

threads.answer:
November 24, 2021 8:50 AM
RE: Implied status for A70 applicants -- REP-2021-2194
QuEsTIoN: Can you please advise whether an applicant under the SCLPC who also submits an application for open work permit under LMIA exemption code A70 can begin working as soon as the application is sent to
IRCC
RESPONSE: Please note that status and authorization are two separate things. In addition, IRCC has stopped using the term 'implied' which is erroneous and replaced it with the term 'maintained' which is more accuarate.
Subsection 30(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act states that:
A foreign national may not work or study in Canada unless authorized to do so under this Act. Section 196 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) states: A foreign national must not work in Canada unless authorized to do so by a work permit or these Regulations. Section 186 of the IRPR provides authorization to work without a permit for specific situations or the issuance, not application, of a work permit authorizes a foreign national to work.
If a person holds a valid work permit at the time they submit an application for an open work permit as a member of the Spouse or Common-law Partner class (SCLPC) then, the application for the open work permit is a renewal under R201. If the foreign national meets the other requirements in paragraph R186(u), they may work without a permit under the conditions of their existing work permit.
If the person apply for permanent residence under SCLPC does not hold a valid work permit at the time of application, then they must wait until a final decision is made on their open work permit application and they receive a work permit.

Best regards,
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
In order to claim points for an arranged employment, the LMIA needs to be valid on the date the applicant applies. LMIAs are typically valid for 6 months. Please check the validity date on the document.
If the applicant demonstrates that they have obtained a valid job offer in their Express Entry profile, they will automatically be awarded additional points towards their CRS score. If they received an ITA based on a provincial nomination by claiming 600 points for a valid job offer from a Canadian employer, they need to provide proof that the offer is legitimate by providing:
- A letter from the employer offering the job in Canada
- The associated LMIA number, if applicable
The Ministerial Instructions list the Minimum Entry Criteria (MEC) for Express Entry. Applicants must meet the MEC to be accepted into the Express Entry pool, and must continue to meet the MÈC when issued an invitation to apply (ITA) and submit their application for permanent residence and their supporting documentations should corroborate their claims. The Express Entry applicant can obtain CRS points for a qualifying offer of arranged employment as long as they meet the requirements as defined under section 29(2) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system.

Applicant must have a valid Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) on the date the application is submitted. The job offer is based on an opinion provided to the officer by the Department of Employment and Social Development. If applicant does not have a valid LMIA at the time they submitted their application, they cannot obtain CRS points for a qualifying offer of an arranged employment. This may result in a loss of CRS points that could bring the rank below the lowest ranked score in the round of invitations under the Express Entry Comprehensive Ranking System.

threads.subject: Question about education equivalency -- REP-2021-2214
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to get clarification on education requirements for PR programs.
If an applicant passes GED high school equivalency certification in Canada, will it be considered equivalent to
Canadian secondary school diploma for the purpose of Permanent Residence applications?
Thank you for your assistance.
Regards,
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: If an applicant passes GED high school equivalency certification in Canada, will it be considered equivalent to Canadian secondary school diploma for the purpose of Permanent Residence applications?
Answer:
Pursuant to R73.1, a Canadian educational credential means any secondary school diploma or any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential, issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational
or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising
and regulating such institutions.
The GED is an internationally recognized test that can be used to support an application for admission to an educational or training program, or to obtain employment. The GED does not meet the requirements of R73.1.
We trust that this information will assist you.

Immigration Representatives Mailbox

This includes all the essential duties and most of the main duties listed. If they are selected under the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) class, they need to continue working for the employer who offered them arranged employment through to visa issuance or the points for FSW (out of 67) will be removed.

The job offer must be in writing, and must set out details of the job the employer is offering such as the pay and deductions, job duties, conditions of employment (hours of work).
Question 3: The employer makes the TFW an offer of employment that meets all the requirements of IRPR 82 (1).
Answer 3: There are few different ways for applicants to obtain points for arranged employment. threads.subject: Afghanistan-overseas dependent of protected person
threads.question:
Afghan national made inland refugee claim in Canada in 2019 and at the time had son overseas who was 21 years old. Afghan national was accepted as protected person in 2021 and overseas son is now 23. Can the
protected person in Canada include his 23-year old overseas son in the Permanent Residence application?
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
November 26, 2021 10:57 AM
RE: Afghanistan-overseas dependent of protected person -- REP-2021-2242
As per R25.1(9), the lock-in date for the age of a child of a person who has submitted a claim for refugee protection inside Canada under subsection 99(3) of the Act, who has acquired protected person status, and who has made an application for permanent residence is the date on which the claim for refugee protection was made. This applies to permanent residence applications received on or after August 1, 2014.
Although the age is locked in at the time of the refugee claim, the applicable definition of "dependent child" is the one that is in effect at the time IRCC receives the complete application for permanent residence from the principal applicant. In your case, the definition of dependent child is under 22 years of age and not a spouse or common-law partner.
For example, in the following case, the child qualifies as a dependent child:
- A permanent residence application is received on July 7, 2019 (the applicable definition is “under 22 years of age").
- A child included in the application is 24 years old when the application is received.
- On the day the refugee claim was made, the child was 21 years old.
For more information, please refer to dependent child lock-in dates by immigration category on the IRCC website.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
If a client who was authorized to work as a refugee claimant, then has their refugee claim refused, does not apply to the RAD and has their judicial review application of the negative refugee claim refused, and therefore has a removal order in force, is issued work permits by IRCC despite section 209 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, are these work permits valid, authorizing the client to work?

If a work permit that was issued by the IRCC during the period in which a removal order was enforceable for this client is not valid, does applying for a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment Application, which makes the removal order unenforceable, then bring the previously invalid work permit into validity? In other words, does a work permit that was invalid due to s 209 become valid, authorizing a client to work, following the successful application of a PRRA? Or should the client apply for a new work permit?
threads.answer:
As per paragraph R209 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulation, a work permit becomes invalid when it expires or when a removal order that is made against the permit holder becomes enforceable. Subsection A49(2) provides the requirements for a removal order against a claimant to become ‘in force’. Section A48 states when a removal order is enforceable.
By policy, IRCC has allowed foreign nationals under an enforceable removal order to remain working in Canada through the issuance of a work permit. In addition, work permits issued prior to a removal order coming into force, remain valid as authorization to work in Canada as long as the foreign national is unable to depart Canada through no fault of their own. This ensures that they do not become a burden on Canadian social services.

IRCC allows the work permit to remain valid when the Government of Canada is unable to remove the foreign national through no fault of the person. For example, the foreign national provides any documents needs to obtain their passport or travel document but their country of citizenship refuses to issue it. You may review the publically available instructions for officers, here: Persons under an unenforceable removal order for further information
We trust you will find this information useful.
Regards,

Please find below the answers to your questions
1. After a student has completed his/her final exams to complete the last semester and finish studies, and a time before DLl issues his/her completion letter or any other communication to indicate completion of studies top allow a student to apply for Post Graduate Work Permit:
a. Would this time period be considered a scheduled break during which a student is allowed to work more than 20 hours? Response: No. To be considered a regularly scheduled break, the break must be part of the DLl's academic calendar (for instance, winter and summer holidays and/or Reading Week). Each regularly scheduled break should not be longer than 150 days. The maximum cumulative duration of scheduled breaks is 180 days per calendar year.
b. Would this time period be considered a scheduled break during which a student is only allowed to work 20 hours or less? Response: This time period is not considered a scheduled break. Students who are eligible to work may work (following the conditions on their study permit) until the first date they receive written confirmation of program completion from their educational institution (for instance, an email, a letter, a transcript or a diploma), provided their study permit remains valid during this period.
c. What if the student was in part time standing in the final semester to take a single course required for graduation-would a student be allowed to work 20 hours during the above stated time period?
d. What if the student was in part time standing in the final semester to take a single course required for graduation-would a student be allowed to work more than 20 hours during the above stated time period? There are no restrictions on the number of hours students can work on campus [as per R186(f)] in addition to working off campus, provided they continue to meet the applicable eligibility requirements. This applies during a student's last semester, even if they are only attending part-time as long as all other conditions are being met. More information can be found here

threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am a lawyer in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario. Would studying online in Canada require a study permit, if the program of study (over 6 months) has both online and in-person components? For example, if the first semester is online and the person is in Canada as a visitor, would they require a study permit to complete the first semester online?
Thank you in advance.
Best regards,
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
mation disclosed under the Access to Information Act
mmigration, Refugees mmigration, Réfugiés
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
All foreign nationals are required to obtain a study permit for engaging in academic, professional, vocational or other education or training that is more than 6 months in duration at a designated learning institution (DLl) in Canada. If the duration of the program is more than 6 months, a study permit will be required even if the first semester is online.
As a consequence of COVID-19, many programs that normally require in-person classes (or in-class learning) have been shifted to an online format. Prospective students who wish to begin a program of study that normally requires in-person attendance at a DLl are advised to apply for a study permit before commencing their studies online, as the program of study may still require the student to be in Canada in the future (subject to travel restrictions). The letter of acceptance or a supporting document from the DLl must clearly indicate that the program requires in-person attendance for the student to complete their program of study once the DLl is able to resume classroom operations. The DLl must also indicate a target start date for courses that require the student to be in Canada. Officers should be satisfied that the applicant intends to continue their studies or complete their program of study in Canada once the DLl resumes classroom operations. However, if there is evidence indicating that the entire program of study has been shifted to distance learning indefinitely and in-person attendance is not essential to complete the program, then the prospective student will not be eligible to apply for a study permit, since physical presence in Canada is not required.
We hope this information is helpful for you.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Bonjour,
Nous avons une interrogation relativement à l'apprentissage à distance pour les étudiants étrangers.
Il est indiqué sur le site d'IRCC que les étudiants suivant des cours à distance, mais ayant une portion du programme en présentiel doivent soumettre une demande pour l'obtention d'un permis d'études. Le permis d'études ne sera toutefois délivré que pour la période des cours en présentiel (voir [https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-](https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-) citoyennete/organisation/publications-guides/bulletins-guides-operationnels/residents-temporaires/permis- etudes/autres-considerations.html)
Cette dernière affirmation nous soulève deux interrogations :
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Bonjour,
Selon ce qui est indiqué icì, un étranger doit obtenir un permis d’études pour entreprendre des études ou des cours de formation universitaire ou professionnelle ou d’autres cours lorsque la durée de ceux-ci est de plus de 6 mois et qu’ils sont donnés dans un établissement d'enseignement désigné (EED) au Canada. Les activités suivantes ne sont pas des études au sens de la Loi sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés (LIPR) et n’exigent pas de permis d’études : les cours préscolaires (prématernelle);
les cours d’intérêt général ou d’autoperfectionnement;
l'apprentissage à distance; les cours suivis à titre d’auditeur libre (généralement des cours théoriques que l’on suit sans obtenir des crédits ou sans avoir la capacité d’obtenir rétroactivement des crédits).
Pour un apprentissage à distance, si la totalité du programme d'études a une durée de plus de six mois, les étudiants doivent obtenir un permis d'études pour la partie du programme offerte au Canada, même si la durée de la partie au Canada est de moins de six mois. La durée du permis d'études ne doit correspondre qu'à la durée de la partie offerte au Canada et cela sera à l’agent d’en déterminer en fonction des documents qui lui seront présentés.
Nous espérons que ces informations vous seront utiles.

threads.subject: Implied Status and Restoration Applications -- REP-2021-2278
threads.question:
Hi,
I have a question about how restoration of status works where a refused extension application is set aside on judicial review.
The scenario is:
Foreign National with a visitor record submits an application from within Canada to change their status from visitor to worker before their visitor record expires (the “Extension and Work Permit Application”). The Extension and Work Permit Application gives them implied status;
IRCC refuses the Extension and Work Permit Application. The client applies for judicial review;
The Foreign National also applies for restoration of status to visitor within ninety days (the “Restoration Application");
The Extension and Work Permit Application refusal is set aside as a result of the judicial review. IRCC re-opens the Extension and Work Permit Application.
IRCC then approves the Restoration Application for a period of thirty days, issuing a visitor record.
I am trying to determine when the person must leave Canada by. Can they remain in Canada beyond the validity period in the new visitor record that was issued as a result of the Restoration Application since their original Extension Application has been re-opened? Does the re-opening of the Extension and Work Permit Application basically render the Restoration Application a nullity?
The IRCC website discusses what happens where two applications are submitted during processing and how a decision on the first application impacts the second application. It does not appear to discuss what happens when the second application is decided before the first, which is what has occurred here as a result of the Extension Application being re-opened.
[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/temporary-residents/visitors/implied-status-extending-stay.html
I hope the above makes sense. Please let me know if it does not.
Sincerely,
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
QUESTION: Can they remain in Canada beyond the validity period in the new visitor record that was issued as a result of the Restoration Application since their original Extension Application has been re-opened? Does the re-opening of the Extension and Work Permit Application basically render the Restoration Application a nullity?
RESPONSE: For clarity, IRCC no longer uses the term 'implied status', this is because status received by operation of law under R183(5) is legal and real. The Department has moved to using the term 'maintained status' to better reflect the real nature of the status.
While your question appears somewhat case specific, we will answer with a general answer and a theoretical case.
01 JAN 2020: A foreign national in Canada without authority to work submits the IMM 5710 Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker. This application would be a two in one-application for extension of status under R181 and application for authority to work under R200. 15 FEB 2020: Initial status expires. As per R183(5) the foreign national's temporary resident status is maintained until a decision is made on the application.
20 FEB 2020: Application is refused-status ends. 25 FEB 2020: Judicial review application submitted. – no effect on status 10 MAR 2020: Application for restoration submitted – no effect on status 15 APR 2020: Retoration of status is approved status is now valid to 14 MAY 2020 01 MAY 2020: The Extension and Work Permit Application refusal is set aside as a result of the judicial review. IRCC re- opens the Extension and Work Permit Application. - since the first application is now open with no final decision, status under R183(5) would again be in effect until a final decision is made. 14 MAY 2020: Visitor Record expires.
The foreign national would be on maintained status from the date the application is re-opened after the judicial review until a new final decision is made. The expiry of the Visitor record would have no effect on the maintained status.

2) With respect to the new policy that international students are not able to from principal applicant to dependent (see: Public policy, competitiveness and economy [R205(c)(ii) - C41, C42, C43, C44, C45] - Canadian interest-International Mobility Program-Canada.ca) please advise if this applies to cases where work permit applications using a PNP certificate. Please refer to the below blurb in considering your response. Response: The update is not new, this is a clarification of an existing policy. For your example, the spouse
(study permit holder) of a provincial nominee who is now the dependent spouse not applying for a work permit based on the (previously) dependent spouse's C41 open work permit, is eligible to apply for a C41 open work permit. The principal foreign national is the first foreign national of the couple who obtained a study or work permit or was deemed authorized to work under the provisions of section R186 other than under paragraph R186(w).

The principal foreign national cannot obtain a spousal open work permit under the C41 or C42 category based on the dependent spouse's spousal open work permit.

threads.answer:
immigration Kepresentatives / Représentants immigration (IRCC)
Bonjour,
Voir ci-dessous notre réponse à vos questions.
Question 1: Nous comprenons donc que seul le demandeur principal peut obtenir un PTOT. Le conjoint pourrait être admissible à demander un permis de travail ouvert sous le code de dispense d’EIMT C-41 si le
demandeur principal occupe un poste de niveau O, A ou B).
Avant d’être admissible, le demandeur doit avoir reçu un accusé réception « régulier » de sa demande de résidence permanente. Sinon, il doit demander un permis de travail fermé sous le code de dispense A-75.
Merci de nous corriger si ce n’est pas le cas.
Réponse à la question 1: Pour les époux ou conjoints de fait de titulaires d'un certificat de sélection du Québec (CSQ), si le demandeur principal étranger a reçu un permis de travail lié à un employeur donné à titre de titulaire d'un CSQ [code de dispense A75 de l’EIMī – province de destination : Québec], peu importe le niveau de compétence de la profession, un permis de travail ouvert pour conjoint peut être approuvé.
Le permis de travail du demandeur principal doit être valide pendant 6 mois après la présentation de la demande de permis de travail ouvert pour conjoint. La période de validité du permis de travail ouvert pour conjoint doit être la même que celle du permis de travail du demandeur principal étranger ou prendre fin à la date d’expiration du passeport ou du titre de voyage de l'époux ou conjoint de fait, selon la première éventualité.
La demande de permis de travail ouvert pour conjoint peut être présentée à partir du Canada ou de l’étranger, en même temps que la demande de permis de travail du demandeur principal étranger ou après.
Pour de plus amples informations, voir la section époux ou conjoints de fait de titulaires d'un CSQ-Politique générale, compétitivité et économie [R205c)(ii) - C41. C42, C43, C44, C45] - Intérêt canadien-Programme de mobilité internationale.
Question 2:
Par contre, plusieurs de nos clients nous relatent d’avoir entendu d’un agent du centre d’appel ou d’un agent frontalier qu’un demandeur pouvait demander le PTOT avec un CSQ et un accusé réception temporaire de la demande de RP.
Merci de confirmer si le fait d’avoir reçu un accusé réception temporaire répond au critère d’avoir subi une vérification de l'exhaustivité de la demande de RP.
Réponse à la question 2: Non, le fait d’avoir reçu un accusé réception temporaire ne répond pas au critère d’avoir subi une vérification de l’exhaustivité de la demande de RP. Le demandeur principal doit soumettre une copie de la lettre d'accusé de réception qui confirme que sa demande de RP est complète.
Question 3:
Un client qui a récemment passé à la frontière Canada/États-Unis nous relate également qu’un agent
frontalier/d’immigration lui avait confirmé oralement que son enfant à charge devenu majeur durant le traitement de sa demande de RP est éligible au PTOT.
Merci de confirmer si de nouvelles directives ont été mises en vigueur afin de permettre maintenant aux enfants à charge majeurs inclus dans la demande de RP des parents de pouvoir obtenir un permis de travail dans l’attente de la confirmation de RP.
Réponse à la question 3: Seul le demandeur principal dans une demande de RP peut présenter une demande de PTOT s’il répond à tous les critères sous cette dispense.
Nous espérons que ces renseignements vous seront utiles.
Cordialement.

threads.question: Please note that CSQs are valid for 2 years whereas PR applications are processed on over 2 years. At the time the CoPR is validated, it is impossible for CSQs to still be valid. Can you please clarify the point below?
threads.answer:
The CSQ must be valid when the applicant submits an application for permanent residence to IRCC (Centralized Intake Office [CIO] in Sydney). If the applicant's CSQ expires before the receipt of the application at the CIO, the application is incomplete and must be returned to the applicant. application by IRCC.

If the application was made within the 36-month deadline, the CSQ will be considered valid until a decision is rendered on the permanent residence application.

RE: NOA Requirements in Parents/Grandparents Program -- REP-2021-1561
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox.
The requirement for sponsors to provide NOAs or an equivalent document as issued by the Minister of National Revenue for the 3 taxation years immediately preceding the date of their sponsorship application is mandatory.
Co-signers are required to meet the same requirements as sponsors, regardless of how long they have been married to or living in a common-law relationship with the sponsor. This means co-signers must also submit NOAs or an equivalent document as issued by the Minister of National Revenue for the three taxation years immediately preceding the date of the sponsorship application in order for their income to be included in the Minimum Necessary Income assessment.
Combined proof of income between the sponsor and co-signer (e.g. 2 years of NOAs submitted by the sponsor and 3 years of NOAs submitted by the co-signer) would not meet the requirements under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations.
We hope you find this information useful.
Thank you,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox (IRCC)

Good day,
The letter of introduction issued to visa-exempt parents and grandparents can be used for multiple entries during its validity.
Anyone in Canada who has valid temporary status may apply to extend their stay by submitting an application before their current status expires: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html).
Temporary resident status and visa are two completely different things. Temporary resident status is granted once a foreign national is authorized to enter Canada at a port of entry. Generally speaking, a super visa holder (meaning they have a super visa counterfoil in their passport or a super visa letter of introduction) will be granted entry for two years and therefore they have temporary resident status for two years. It is this status that expires, not the visa. The expiry date on the visa counterfoil in the passport is the date that the visa expires and is the last day on which the foreign national can travel to and/or enter Canada.
And finally, super visa holders do not have to live in the same household with the inviter child or the grandchild; however, the inviter is still responsible for financially supporting their parents/grandparents throughout their stay in Canada.
Best regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
Hello,
A foreign national initially entered into Canada on August 21, 2021 as a visitor, and currently is in Canada with a valid status until February 21, 2022.
She is planning to take a 4 months ESL course at a private language school (DLI) from December 1, 2021 until March 31, 2022, however, she has less than 3 months left until her current visitor status expires.
Is she allowed to complete her 4 month course with the end date on March 31, 2022, which is later than 6 months after her initial entry to Canada, provided that she maintains her visitor status by applying for an extension before her current status expiration?

threads.answer:
Good day,
Please see below the approved response.
If she is able to maintain her visitor status by applying for an extension and receives a positive response before her current status expiration, she will be allowed to complete the 4 month course.
Foreign nationals are required to obtain a study permit for engaging in academic, professional, vocational or other education or training that is more than 6 months in duration at a designated learning institution (DLl) in Canada. In this case, this foreign national does not need a study permit but still needs to have a valid status to be allowed to stay in Canada.

threads.subject: Authorized Leave and Authorization to Work -- REP-2021-2178
threads.question:
Dear IRCC representatives,
I hope my message finds you well. Could you please help me with an Authorized Leave question? We have a student in a 2-year PGwP-eligible program whose record looks like this:
Full-time in every mandatory term until Fall 2021
Fall 2021 – approved Authorized Leave
Winter 2022 – enrolled part-time. This is their last term
My question would be whether the student is authorized to work part-time in Winter 2022 and after they
apply for a PGWP.
Technically, students on an Authorized Leave don't have courses. However, they are still compliant with the PGWP requirements. Does this make the student eligible to work in Winter 2022 and after they apply for a PGWP considering that they met all the other requirements? Would being on an Authorized Leave be equal to maintaining full-time status?
The manuals don't specifically cover this part, that's why I wasn't sure how to interpret the regulation.
RE: working part-time in the final term, the manual reads:
Students who have maintained full-time status for the duration of their program of study, and who only require a part-time course load in their final academic session in order to complete their program of study, are allowed to work full-time during the regularly scheduled break before their last semester and are allowed to work off campus up to 20 hours per week during their final academic session.
RE: working after applying for a PGWP, the manual reads:
Students who have completed their program of study are allowed to work (under paragraph 186(w) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations [IRPR]) while they are waiting for a decision on their post-graduation work permit application, provided they meet all of the following criteria:
they are or were holders of a valid study permit at the time of the post-graduation work permit application they were a full-time student enrolled at a DLI in a post-secondary academic, vocational or professional training program they were authorized to work off-campus without a work permit they did not exceed the allowable hours of work
Thank you and looking forward to your reply. Have a great day.
Best regards,
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
Students must maintain their full-time student status during each academic session of the program or programs of study they complete and submit as part of their post-graduation work permit application. However, if a student meets all the eligibility requirements, with the exception of full-time status during their final academic session (that is, they have part-time status only in their academic session), they are still considered eligible for the PGWPP.
The exception is for their final academic session only. If the student was on an Authorized leave in Fall 2021 and enrolled part-time for Winter 2022, the student is allowed to work during their final semester and after applying for their PGWP assuming all other eligibility criteria has been met. Please note that when the student applies for PGWP they will need to include the documentation from the DLI indicating that the leave was authorized and reasons for leave.
We hope that this information is helpful to you. Thank you
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
