threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
migration, Réfugiés
Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case specific advice.
Scenario: Applicant XX worked in Canada with an LMIA-based Work Permit for over one year and is currently employed under the same condition. Now, his LMIA work permit has ~11 months left before expiry, and XX plans to apply through the EE-CEC class. His current employer has signed a new valid job offer and promised him a permanent position if XX receives PR. Therefore, he wants to claim the additional 50 points on the “offer of employment” in the Express Entry System.
Question: Could you please clarify on “authorized to work"? For the above scenario:
1. Must XX's LMIA-based Work Permit be valid up until he_is accepted as a permanent resident of Canada? Or
2. Instead, can the applicant switch to an open work permit, say bridging work permit (BOWP), after submitting the CEC-PR application and before his LMIA work permit expires?
3. If he does change to BOWP, will this result in his offer of employment in the EE application being invalid?
Answer 1: The foreign national is “authorized to work" in Canada when they hold a valid work permit, valid on the date on which their application for permanent resident visa is made and on the date on which the visa is issued. To get points for the arranged employment, the work permit must be issued and valid at ITA and lock-in date. Applicants must have worked for the employer on the work permit for at least one year continuously and meet all other requirements. They must continue to meet the criteria for arranged employment points as per section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system. If applicants demonstrate they have obtained a valid job offer in their Express Entry profile, they will automatically be awarded additional points towards their CRS score.
MIs-Points for qualifying offer of arranged employment 29 (1) If a foreign national has a qualifying offer of arranged employment, they may be assigned points as follows:
- 200 points, if the offer is for employment in an occupation contained in Major Group 00 of the National Occupation Classification matrix; or
- 50 points, if the offer is any other qualifying offer of arranged employment.
If they are selected under the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) class, they need to continue working for the employer who offered them arranged employment through to visa issuance or the points for FSW (out of 67) will be removed. The requirement to claim points for arranged employment in Express Entry are listed on our website.
Answer 2: Applicants may be eligible for a bridging open work permit (BOWP), which lets them continue working while waiting for the results of their permanent residence application. The eligibility guidelines for the Bridging Open Work Permit (BOWP) can be found on our website. One of the parameter of BOWP is that applicants have valid status on a work permit that is due to expire within the next 4 months. Applicants cannot apply for a BOWP on maintained status (previously called implied status).
The following foreign nationals do not qualify for a BOWP:
- foreign nationals in Canada under section R186 who are exempt from the work permit requirement
- foreign nationals who have let their status expire and must apply for restoration to return to temporary resident status
- foreign nationals whose work permits are valid for longer than 4 months or who already have a new LMIA that can be used as the basis for a new work permit application
- foreign nationals applying for a BOWP at a port of entry (POE) or visa office
- spouses and dependents of principal permanent resident applicants
- foreign nationals who are inadmissible to Canada
Answer 3: Applicants are assessed on whether or not they meet the requirements of the program based on the information they provided. We ask applicants that all the work experience should be disclosed as accurately as possible when completing their application for permanent residence. We do not penalize applicants for getting a BOWP after they have applied, as long as they meet the conditions of arranged employment at the time of ITA and lock-in date. Lock-in date
means the application received date by IRCC.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the
applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: URGENT-Question about on-campus work -- REP-2021-2193
threads.question:
Hello,
We have the following question:
A professor wants to hire a foreign student eligible to work on and off campus with his study permit. The work will be done at an affiliated hospital, and the student will be paid exclusively from the professor's research fund.
Can the employer be the hospital directly, or must the employment contract be with We are having divergent opinions here and seek your clarification.
Thank you,
and Citizenship Caneda
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
For on-campus employment, students may work at any number of jobs on campus or as a research or teaching assistant at facilities off campus in research related to their research grant. These facilities can include teaching hospitals, clinics and research institutes that have a formal association or affiliation with the learning institution. So, as long as the research grant has a formal association or affiliation with the DLl, research conducted outside of the physical boundaries of the institution could be considered on-campus employment.
The employer can be any of the following:
the institution a faculty a student organization the students themselves (self-employment taking place on campus) a private business a private contractor providing services to the institution on the campus
Please note that students who have not had an immigration medical examination (IME) as part of their study permit will require one if their off-campus work will be in a hospital or any other area where the protection of public health is essential. For more information, find out who must submit to an immigration medical examination.
We hope that this information is helpful to you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Answer: Please note that work permit eligibility or experience under a work issued under R205(c) C11 exemption is not associate to the eligibility for permanent residence programs, therefore, we are unable to provide guidance on that issue. However, we can confirm that a candidate may qualify under the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) program if they have one year of continuous work as a self-employed person. If invited to apply, individuals must be prepared to substantiate all work experience claimed in their profile and provide evidence that their claimed experience corresponds to the occupational description(s) as set out in the NOC codes they have specified. If a candidate is considered self-employed pursuant to paragraph 15(7)(b) of the MIs and paragraph 87.1(3)(b) of the Regulations, periods of self-employment do not count for purposes of CRS points for “Canadian work experience” or meeting the work experience requirement under the CEC.
In order to qualify for points for arranged employment, pursuant to Section 29(2)(a)(ii) and Section 29(2)(a)(ii) - a foreign national must work for an employer, in an employer-employee relationship, and the offer itself must be made by the employer to an employee. Generally, self-employment would not fall under either section 29 of Ministerial Instructions.
The assessment of an individual's employment status must necessarily be undertaken on a case-by-case basis, considering their particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. threads.subject: Qs re Validity of the Visitor Record -- REP-2021-2400
threads.question:
From ## Dear team,
My name is
A client came to Canada in July 2019 and later filed for a visitor record, which was approved for 2 years up to 27-Dec-2021. In between, she had visited India for a period of 20 days in March 2021 and returned back to Canada. Can she use the same visitor record (issued previously) to remain in Canada until 27-Dec-2021?
Or does the visitor record invalidate after leaving Canada?
Can you please also share any official links that say that the Visitor Record does not get invalidated after leaving Canada?
I respectfully thank you in advance for your assistance.
Thank you.
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
Good day,
A visitor record is a status document issued to visa-required or visa-exempt foreign nationals who are seeking to enter or are in Canada. It specifies the conditions and validity period of their temporary stay in Canada. A foreign national's temporary resident status ends on their departure from Canada. If on return the officer determines that they meet requirements of A22, the person becomes a temporary resident. If the Border Services Officer is going to grant entry to the foreign national, they will either re-admit the foreign national on the original VR or they can choose to take the VR from the client and give them the standard 6 months (or other duration).
If there is no stamp or handwritten date in the foreign national's passport, their authorized period of stay is 6 months from the day they initially entered Canada, or until their passport expires, whichever comes first, as per subsection R183(2).
More information about the Visitor Record document, visit the following site: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html)
Thank you,

Date: Friday, December 10, 2021 at 8:39 PM ### Dear
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representative Mailbox. Note that we cannot reply to case-specific scenarios.
To be eligible for permanent residence under stream A of the temporary public policy for Hong Kong residents, applicants must have graduated from a post-secondary designated learning institution in Canada, obtained eligible credentials as indicated on our website, and must have completed at least 50% of the program while physically present in Canada, either in person (in class) or online. Applicants may be eligible if the program of study was completed through distance learning while being physically present in Canada for at least 50% of the program of study and while being legally authorized to study in Canada.
Since by definition distance learning does not require one to be in Canada, a study permit cannot be issued for this type of course. For example, if a foreign national authorized to work in Canada is prohibited from engaging in studies as per a condition of their work permit, they are allowed to engage in distance learning courses. However, some distance learning courses include an in-Canada portion to the program (e.g., special tutorials or the writing of final exams). If the overall course of study is greater than six months, then the student requires a study permit for the in-Canada portion of the program, even if the in-Canada portion is less than six months.
We trust this information will assist you.

threads.answer:
Paper Passport Requirement -- REP-2021-2249
Hello, Please see our response to your question.
Question: I represent a US citizen who lives in upstate New York and would seek entry to Canada overland at a land border between New York State and Ontario. In 2021, he was found to qualify for a work permit under the International Experience Class (Recognized Organization-SWAP) Program. He was later disqualified from the program by SWAP in Toronto, as he did not hold a paper US passport book but rather a US passport card. The Director of SWAP in Canada advised that a US citizen must hold paper passport book to qualify for a work permit under the IEC Program and SWAP. He would not be boarding an aircraft to travel to Canada, but crossing overland in a private vehicle.
As you are aware, as American citizens do not need passports to travel to Canada overland. The client in this instance is from a community in upstate New York that is less than 10 minutes from the Canadian border. Hence, he would not fly to Canada under any circumstances.
As the IEC work permit approval is issued by electronic letter and then presented to the CBSA at the port of entry for work permit issuance on arrival in Canada, it is unclear why a paper booklet passport requirement would be imposed by SWAP. For reference also note:
Section 52 of the IRPR regulations states: Documents — temporary residents
52 (1) In addition to the other requirements of these Regulations, a foreign national seeking to become a temporary resident must hold one of the following documents that is valid for the period authorized for their stay:
o (a) a passport that was issued by the country of which the foreign national is a citizen or national, that does not prohibit travel to Canada and that the foreign national may use to enter the country of issue;
o (b) a travel document that was issued by the country of which the foreign national is a citizen or national, that does not prohibit travel to Canada and that the foreign national may use to enter the country of issue;
Under R52(1), the USA citizen holding a passport card complies with R52(1) (a) and (b). As it is not a legal requirement for Americans to hold a paper booklet passport to secure a work permit for Canada, can you explain why SWAP is disqualifying US citizens who do not hold paper passports?
Answer:
We can confirm that a U.S. passport card is a document accepted by both IRCC and CBSA as acceptable proof of U.S. citizenship for the purposes of both travel to Canada, and for use when submitting a work permit application.
SWAP has been informed by our department that a U.S. passport card is considered a document that is suitable to prove work authorized status for employment eligibility verification processes. If not already done, we recommend the client to reach out to SWAP and they will assist them in their application.
We hope this information is of assistance.
Thank you kindly.

threads.subject: Demande de précisions sur les emplois du domaine de la santé soumis à l'exigence
threads.question:
Bonjour Madame, Monsieur,
Nous sommes les représentants de la firme d’avocats en droit d’immigration Nous venons par ce courriel obtenir plus de précisions sur les emplois du domaine de la santé soumis à l’exigence des examens médicaux. Existe-t-il une liste exhaustive ou non? Certains emplois du domaine de la santé, tels en santé naturelle qui requièrent seulement des conseils à distance (sans
contact avec le patient) sont-ils soumis à l’exigence des examens médicaux?
Dans l’espoir d’une réponse à nos questions, recevez Madame, Monsieur, nos sincères salutations.
Bien à vous !
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
des examens médicaux. -- REP-2021-2295
Bonjour,
Les requérants qui souhaitent travailler dans un établissement de soins de santé, y compris dans le domaine de la santé naturelle, doivent compléter un Examen médical à des fins d’immigration (EMI), car leur profession les amène à travailler auprès de personnes présentant des conditions de santé vulnérables et où la protection de la santé publique est essentielle. Les requérants travaillant à distance doivent également se soumettre à l’exigence de l’EMi, car le requérant se trouve dans un contexte où, s'il devait retourner dans son environnement de travail, il serait en contact étroit avec des individus présentant des conditions de santé les rendant particulièrement vulnérables. Puisque nous ne savons pas si le requérant retournera dans son environnement de travail, même de façon occasionnelle, le risque pour
la santé publique est trop grand.
Merci,
La boîte aux lettres des représentants de l'immigration

threads.subject: Caregiver LMIA-based Work Permit Application
threads.question:
Dear Officer,
According to the June 18, 2019 Ministerial Instructions ([https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/work-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/work-) without-permit/changes-work-permits-issued-caregivers/refusal-to-process.html), IRCC will not process LMIA work permit if all of a list of criteria apply. One of those criteria include “the applicant is making an initial work permit application", which suggests that applicants who are applying for a work permit inside Canada will have their applications processed.
Could you clarify whether an applicant who previously held a work permit, applied to extend their work permit before their status expired, and is currently in Canada on maintained status is eligible to apply for a work permit inside Canada supported by a Caregiver LMIA?
Best,
Lim.Elina
threads.answer:
December 23, 2021 1:12 PM
RE: Caregiver LMIA-based Work Permit Application -- REP-2021-2454
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox.
The program delivery instructions provide that officers must not process applications for new LMIA-required
work permits made by foreign nationals under subparagraph 200(1)(c)(i) of the Immigration and Refugee
Protection Regulations (IRPR) if all of the following criteria apply:
- The intended occupation is in National Occupational Classification (NOC) 4411 (excluding foster parents) or 4412 (excluding housekeepers). The applicant is outside Canada. The applicant is making an initial work permit application (that is, they do not currently hold a valid work permit). The applicant is destined to a job location outside Quebec. The accompanying LMIA application has been received by Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) on or after June 18, 2019.
The refusal to process Mis do not apply if an applicant previously held a work permit, applied to extend their work permit before their status expired, and is currently in Canada on maintained status.
Thanks,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Students can complete up to 100% of their studies online from outside Canada. threads.answer:
December 24, 2021 9:52 AM Sent: RE: Question -- REP-2021-2250
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Scenario: An applicant has been working for the an employer for about two months now. Earlier in 2018 to 2019, he has worked for the same employer for over over year in the same occupation while holding an open work permit. Then he went back to France. He came back recently with an employer-specific work permit, issued based on the LMIA exemption C 16, with the support of the same employer.
In order to claim 10 points under the FSW for arranged employment, the guidelines state: if you have a valid work permit for a NOC 0, A or B job that is exempt from needing an LMIA, and you:
- are currently working for an employer specified on the work permit
- have one year of full-time work experience (or an equal amount of part-time work) for that employer
- have a valid job offer from that employer for at least one year after we issue your permanent resident visa
Question: The applicant has worked for the same employer for over 1 year in the past and he is currently working for the employer specified on the work permit. He also holds a full-time indeterminate job offer. However, his initial work experience isn't continuous to present, even though it still the same occupation and employer. And he didn't have an employer-specific work permit at the time of that work experience. In this scenario, would he be eligible to claim 10 points for holding a valid job offer?
Answer: To be eligible for the Federal Skilled Worker Class, applicants must have at least one year of continuous, paid work experience within the last ten years in the same NOC as the job as is being used in the application. If they are selected under the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) class, they need to continue working for the employer who offered them arranged employment through to visa issuance or the points for FSW (out of 67) will be removed.
In order to obtain points for arranged employment, applicants must continue to meet the criteria for arranged employment as per section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system on the date they receive their invitation to apply and on the date they applied for permanent residence. If invited to apply, applicants must be prepared to substantiate all work experience claimed in their profile and provide evidence that their claimed experience corresponds to the occupational description(s) as set out in the NOC codes they have specified.
Applicants must also meet all these requirements to be awarded job offer points when the applicant is in possession of an employer-specific, LMIA-exempt work permit: ● the foreign national must currently hold a valid work permit issued under the circumstances described in paragraph 204(a) or (c) or section 205 of the Regulations,
- the job offer is made by an employer who is specified on the work permit;
- the foreign national must currently work for the employer on the work permit;
and Cizenship Canadaot Citoyenneté Canada
●must have accumulated at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, over a continuous period of work in Canada for that employer.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application and an individual's employment is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Note that we can't respond to case-specific scenarios. To be eligible under Stream A of the permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, the applicant must have graduated from a post-secondary designated learning institution (DLl) in Canada in the 3 years before they apply with at least 50% of the program completed while physically present in Canada, either in person or online. To find out is a Diploma of Vocational Studies (DVS) is a considered to be a post-secondary diploma, applicants are advised to verify with their educational institution.
2. Would an applicant with one of the above qualifying education requirements completed from Quebec but presently residing in another province be able to apply through the temporary public policy if the applicant can provide sufficient proof of intent to continue residing in a province or territory other than Quebec? The fact that an applicant completed their studies in Quebec does not, conclusively, suggest that the applicant does not intend to reside in another province or territory as a permanent resident. On the other hand, the fact that an applicant currently resides in a province or territory other than Quebec at the time of application also does not, conclusively, suggest that the applicant intends to reside in that province or territory as a permanent resident. The onus is on the applicant to provide sufficient proof to satisfy the officer that they intend to reside outside Quebec. Evidence that applicants intend to reside outside Quebec can include, but is not limited to,
an employment reference
- job offers or jobs applied to or interviewed for family ties •a lease agreement or property ownership a statutory declaration
We trust this information will assist you.
